attorneys.name: C.D. Taylor Pace
attorneys.practice_type: Risk Management & Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Taylor Pace has been practicing defense litigation in the firm's Raleigh office since the inception of the firm. He and Paul Cranfill co-chair the firm's Workers’ Compensation Group.

Taylor received his B.A. degree from the University of North Carolina in 1982, graduating with Phi Beta Kappa honors. He received his J. D. degree from the University of North Carolina School of Law in 1985.

During the first several years of his practice, Taylor was involved not only in the defense of workers’ compensation claims before the Industrial Commission, but also in the defense of general civil litigation Superior Court matters, trying jury cases to verdicts in the areas of automobile negligence, products liability, and premises liability.

In more recent years, Taylor has focused his practice on the defense of employers and insurance carriers in workers’ compensation claims. He has represented employers and carriers at all levels of workers’ compensation litigation, including mediations, hearings before Deputy Commissioners, appeals before the Full Commission, as well as appeals before both the Court of Appeals and Supreme Court. In addition to his practice before the Industrial Commission, Taylor also represents clients in State and Federal courts in lawsuits involving third party workers’ compensation liens as well as Woodson liability.

When the North Carolina Bar Association established its Workers’ Compensation Section in 1995 (which is now comprised of more than 600 attorneys), Taylor was selected as one of the original 15 attorneys to serve on the Section's governing counsel.

Over the years Taylor has been recognized as one of North Carolina's best lawyers in the area of workers’ compensation. He has been listed in the publication "The Best Lawyers in America," for the past few years. Taylor was recognized as one of North Carolina’s “Super Lawyers®" in 2008 and 2009. And for several years, Martindale Hubbell, the nation's most prestigious national peer review publication for lawyers, has issued its highest rating (AV) to Taylor.

attorneys.bio:
Jacksonville, North Carolina State and Federal Criminal Defense Attorney Walter H. Paramore

Criminal defense lawyer Walter Paramore has been in practice for more than 30 years. He focuses on providing quality criminal defense representation to clients facing North Carolina or federal charges, including in death penalty cases.

Since 1995, Mr. Paramore has been certified as a specialist in criminal law by the North Carolina State Bar Board of Legal Specialization. In his years of practice, he has handled in excess of 130 criminal jury trials, 11 capital murder trials and numerous federal appeals.

Attorney Paramore is a senior member of the Criminal Justice Act (CJA) Panel, which consists of attorneys in private practice who are appointed to accept federal criminal cases. This participation, combined with his work as a former prosecutor, has allowed him to build extensive knowledge and experience in the area of criminal defense.

attorneys.name: K. Denise Pardue
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Mount Airy, NC
attorneys.bio:
Denise is an associate in the firm’s litigation practice group. She regularly handles matters involving Criminal Defense, Workers' Compensation and Traffic Violations on behalf of individuals and businesses in Surry and Stokes Counties. In addition to her trial practice, Denise is a member of the North Carolina Advocates for Justice, an organization dedicated to protecting people’s rights, the North Carolina Bar Association and the Surry County Bar Association.

Denise graduated from University of North Carolina at Charlotte in 1989. Following her graduation she worked for the State of North Carolina in the Department of Corrections for 12 years. She then attended Ohio Northern University Pettit College of Law, graduating in 2004. Denise is licensed to practice law in the Commonwealth of Virginia where she practiced for two years before returning home to North Carolina. She joined Royster and Royster in 2006.

Denise is the president of Matthew 25:35, Inc., an organization which raises money to assist people in the community with a specific emphasis on feeding the hungry. The group is involved in an outreach ministry and serves a community meal monthly. Since its formation in 2011, Matthew 25:35, Inc. has either prepared, served, bought or delivered over 250,000 meals in the community.

Outside of the office, Denise enjoys spending time with her family, traveling and organizing fundraising events. She attends Fellowship Baptist Church and serves as a member of the welcome team.

attorneys.name: Corey V. Parton
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Corey Parton is the Founder and Managing Partner at Parton Law, PLLC. He has practiced law in Charlotte, North Carolina, as a civil litigator since 2013.

Attorney Parton has an undergraduate degree in Communications from Virginia Tech. He completed his legal education in two-and-a-half years while receiving Dean’s List Honors. His work experience includes a position in the Pentagon in the Office of the Secretary of Defense for Policy, and on Capitol Hill as a Staff Assistant for the U.S. House of Representatives Committee on Homeland Security. Both positions required him to hold a Top-Secret Security Clearance issued by the U.S. Government.

In 2013, Attorney Parton opened the doors to a successful solo practice in Charlotte: Parton Law Firm. In 2015, he partnered with Chad Buckingham to create Parton Buckingham PLLC, which later became Parton Law, PLLC.

Attorney Parton is active in the Mecklenburg County Bar, having served as Former Chair and Vice-Chair for the Lawyer Referral Service Committee, a Member of the Continuing Legal Education Committee, and a Member of the Lawyer Referral Service Taskforce. His accolades are numerous:

Featured in Fortune & Forbes as a Charlotte Leader in Law;

Recognized as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers nine years in a row;

Selected to Business North Carolina Magazine’s 2025 Legal Elite;

Named a Person on the Move by the Charlotte Business Journal.

Attorney Parton was also honored as the Outstanding Panel Member of the Year by the Mecklenburg County Bar Lawyer Referral Service and is an Inductee of the North Carolina Pro Bono Honor Society.

Attorney Parton has taught Continuing Legal Education courses to his colleagues on Trial Publicity, Rules for Discovery, Advanced Trial Tactics, and Building Cases with Electronic Evidence for National Business Institute, Inc. He has been featured on Charlotte’s WBTV-3 & Time Warner Cable News as a Legal Consultant, recognized with an Outstanding Teacher Award for his volunteer work teaching English as a Second Language to Adults, and has been published by the American Bar Association on Environmental Litigation and Toxic Torts.

Attorney Parton is also the President of the Parton Parkinson's Project, a Charlotte-based 501(c)(3) dedicated to improving lives affected by Parkinson’s disease by hosting charitable events that support nonprofits advancing awareness, research, and resources to empower those living with the disease and progress toward a cure.

Attorney Parton enjoys spending time with his wife and two young children. He is also a die-hard Buffalo Bills fan, which has taught him patience, perseverance, and how to stay true during tough times.

attorneys.bio:
Ed Pauley graduated from West Virginia University in 1988 with a B.A. in political science and received his Juris Doctor from the West Virginia University College of Law in 1991. After law school, Ed practiced in West Virginia concentrating his practice on various types of litigation, including personal injury, medical malpractice, workers’ compensation, railroad litigation, premises liability and asbestos exposure litigation.

Ed joined Wallace & Graham in 1999. He handles workers' compensation, asbestos litigation, personal injury and civil litigation. Ed has handled hundreds of cases before the North Carolina Industrial Commission and appears frequently in appeals before the Full Commission of the NCIC and the North Carolina Court of Appeals.

Admitted to practice in North Carolina, Kentucky, and West Virginia and before the United States Supreme Court, Ed is a member of the American Bar Association and the North Carolina Academy of Trial Lawyers.

The dedication and extensive experience of Mr. Ed Pauley have allowed him to become renowned as a highly effective Charlotte work-related injury lawyer and a talented Charlotte defective medical devices attorney. He employs a variety of litigation, negotiation and mediation strategies to obtain the most favorable outcomes for his clients.

attorneys.name: Barri Hilton Payne
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Durham, NC
attorneys.bio:
Barri Hilton Payne was born in High Point, North Carolina and grew up in Davidson County. She attended the University of North Carolina at Charlotte where she majored in Religious studies and Sociology. Barri practiced for the last twelve years as a founding partner in the firm Brock, Payne & Meece, P.A. before opening her own solo law and mediation practice in 2013.

Barri was involved with the Holderness Moot Court while in law school at UNC and earned her law degree in 1999. She has practiced in Durham, North Carolina since that time and concentrates her practice on family law issues such as divorce, child custody and support, property division and spousal support, with an emphasis towards resolving these issues through alternatives, like mediation designed to minimize conflict for the family. In 2011, Barri became a board certified family law specialist and a certified family financial mediator. She also assists her clients with will preparation, family law appeals, and adoption. She practices primarily in Durham County, but also takes cases in Orange, Chatham, and Wake Counties.

Before beginning law school at the University of North Carolina School of Law, Barri had the opportunity to reside in several different states including Washington, Texas, Georgia, and Alabama. While she enjoyed many of these places, she loves calling North Carolina home. Barri lives in Durham with her husband John and their eight year old daughter Amelia. Her family loves the beach, camping in their RV, and Durham's many attractions such as the Life and Science Museum and the Bulls games. Barri and her family also stay busy with activities at their church.

Barri regularly volunteers with the Legal Information Service through the Compass Center in Chapel Hill, which provides free telephone consultations to clients. Barri has taught seminars for the Compass Center's Free Legal Clinics on the topics of child custody, child support, and spousal support. She is also currently the Chair of the Durham Family Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Julia M. Pendleton
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Julia M. Pendleton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Greensboro, NC
attorneys.bio:
Julia is celebrating year twenty this year as a family law attorney, having graduated in 2005. In 2014, Julia opened her own practice after working with McKinney Perry & Coalter, PA for seven years. Julia was an associate attorney and then promoted to partnership. Julia is a zealous advocate for her clients and enjoys both counseling and litigating. Her caseload over the years has provided invaluable experience in handling issues of separation, divorce and conflict that arises from relationships, especially involving custody of children. Along the way, Julia has learned to manage client expectations and at the same time provide meaningful advice and counsel. Julia's mission is to protect and advise her clients as they go through life-changing experiences, and to do so with professionalism, integrity and compassion.

Julia is a graduate of UNC-Chapel Hill where she double-majored in Journalism and Political Science and then subsequently received her J.D. from Campbell Law School with a concentration in trial advocacy. Julia served as a Student Bar Association representative for her law school class and was also a member of the National Trial Team. Since entering the field of law, Julia has been actively involved in her profession and the community. She has taught classes that focus on court navigation and parenting, and she has also been involved in leadership with the Greensboro Jaycees and Greensboro Junior League in past years.

During her free time, Julia enjoys traveling to Blowing Rock and Hilton Head Island and spending time with her family, including her husband Blake and two dogs Maggie and Thorn.

attorneys.name: K. Clay Pendleton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lincolnton, NC
attorneys.bio:
K. Clay Pendleton is a dedicated family law attorney with over 35 years of legal experience serving clients in Lincoln and Catawba County. Clay is known for providing assertive legal representation and highly responsive client service. He handles a wide range of family law matters - including divorce, child custody, child support, post separation support, alimony, property division, adoption, termination of parental rights, and domestic violence - with the expert strategy, focus and determination needed to protect his client's rights at every stage.

After receiving his undergraduate from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, he received his Juris Doctor from Wake Forest School of Law and was admitted to the North Carolina State Bar in 1987. Thereafter he joined The Pendleton Law Firm and continued the family legacy with his father, Don M. Pendleton.

Known for his client-focused approach, Clay makes accessibility a priority. He provides every client with his personal cell phone number and is committed to being responsive when clients need him most. Whether it's answering a quick question or discussing an urgent issue, clients can count on direct communication and consistent support 7 days a week. Clay is typically able to meet with new or existing clients within 24 to 48 hours and offers weekend appointments when needed. Clients know they can count on him to be there when it matters most.

Outside the office, Clay enjoys spending time with his wife, Carole, and their three children, and values the same family principles in his personal life that he works to protect for his clients.

attorneys.name: Amy L. Pfeiffer
attorneys.practice_type: Alternative Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Following law school, Amy Pfeiffer began her legal career in North Carolina by serving as a law clerk for the Honorable John B. Lewis, Jr. of the North Carolina Court of Appeals for the calendar year January through December 1992.

After a short stint as a legislative assistant for the NC Academy of Trial Lawyers, Amy became involved in NC workers' compensation law in 1993 when she joined the North Carolina Industrial Commission as an Agency Legal Specialist. In 1995, Amy was made a Special Deputy Commissioner, whereby she was responsible for conducting Form 24 administrative hearings. She also ruled on hundreds of medical motions, reviewed thousands of compromise settlement agreements, and traveled throughout the State to talk about the workers' compensation system to various employers and schools. In 1997, she was named a Deputy Commissioner. Amy was a Deputy Commissioner for six years, through 2003, during which time she heard hundreds of cases and filed Opinions & Awards on these cases.

Amy left the Industrial Commission in 2003 and went to work for a year for a plaintiffs' workers' compensation firm. In 2004, she came to Cranfill Sumner & Hartzog where she now represents defendants in workers' compensation cases.

attorneys.name: Joshua Phanco
attorneys.practice_type: Homeowners/Property Owners' Association, Foreclosure and Real Estate Matters Lawyers in Shallotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Joshua Phanco is a highly experienced and accomplished trial attorney with a reputation for going above and beyond in his efforts to secure the best outcome for victims of crime. The son of a federal agent, Joshua moved around a lot growing up. He graduated from Loyola University School of Law in New Orleans in 2009 and was soon recruited to join the Harris County District Attorney's Office in Houston, Texas. In his 10-year career as a prosecutor Joshua has tried more than sixty cases, ranging from DWIs to murders and capital murders. As a felony chief prosecutor in the Major Offenders division he has been tasked with handling extremely complex, high-profile serial killer murders and gang war killings.

Joshua is fond of stating that he is a lawyer because no one will pay him to surf or play guitar, and that is probably because he is not very good at either. A philosophy major in college, Joshua still enjoys reading philosophy books and arguing about the "big questions" of life over lunch. Joshua and his wife, Melinda, are parents to four children and they enjoy spending time together doing outdoors activities and games, all sorts. Joshua and Melinda consider helping people to be their life's mission, and they are always excited to talk about problems or needs that they can help with. Whatever the problem or area of law, Joshua is committed to a life of continual learning and being the best lawyer, and best person, he can be.

attorneys.name: Bonnie F. Pierce
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Greenville, NC
attorneys.bio:
Bonnie Pierce’s introduction to the legal world began in 1993 following the tragic death of her teenage son in a truck crash. Attorney Pierce’s personal tragedy was the spearhead behind the pursuit of her career in law and remains the driving force behind every truck crash she investigates.

Pierce is a dedicated victim’s advocate and promoter of highway safety. She has traveled to Washington D.C. where she testified before lawmakers on the rules governing the hours of service, the need to keep rest areas open, and for tougher laws and stricter enforcement. Pierce began her advocacy work in 1994 as a point of contact in North Carolin for Parents Against Tired Truckers (P.A.T.T.), a grassroots organization made up of families of other truck crash victims which has since united with Citizens for Safe and Reliable Highways (CRASH) to form the Truck Safety Coalition (TSC) which serves as a strong, grassroots, safety advocacy group. Pierce now works with the Institute for Safer Trucking (IST) a nonprofit organization that works hard to raise awareness about truck safety issues, offering support to families impacted by truck crashes, and is committed to making trucking safer across the United States.

attorneys.name: Heather Piercy
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
I am an associate with this firm who focuses my practice on workers’ compensation cases. I am passionate about workers’ compensation cases because I believe that injured employees deserve protection and justice. I also regularly handle personal injury and other civil litigation matters. I have been with the firm for more than four years, and I work on a team with H. Edward “Eddie” Knox, our managing partner.

Earning my Bachelor of Arts in Journalism and Mass Communication at the University of North Carolina, I have a strong background in writing, editing, and public speaking. After Carolina, I went on to complete my Juris Doctor at Charlotte School of Law, receiving the distinction of cum laude on my law degree. While at Charlotte Law, I was inducted into the Order of the Crown.

I am a native of Denver, North Carolina, but have resided in Charlotte for more than five years. I am committed to serving the community in the Queen City and surrounding areas. I am a member of the North Carolina State Bar, the Mecklenburg County Bar, and the Charlotte Women Attorneys. I am an active volunteer for the annual Fighting For Women with Fashion event to benefit the Clyde and Ethel Dickson domestic violence shelter.

Most importantly, I am dedicated to serving as both an attorney and a true counselor for my clients.

See some of Heather’s client reviews below:

“I felt as though I had known Heather my entire life from our first meeting. She is genuine and caring. She went above and beyond the call of duty for me. I cannot say enough good about her.”

-Satisfied Client

“In March of 2011 I was seriously injured at work. I had the cartilage torn completely out of my left hip socket. The doctors that my employer sent me to were dismissive, rude and unprofessional. They said my injury was pre-existing even though I had no pain prior to the accident, and their own radiologist put in his report that there was no evidence of wear and tear to my hip indicating that it was pre-existing. They put me at maximum medical improvement with no treatment whatsoever and said I was fine to return to my job as a paramedic. I was in tremendous pain. I couldn't sleep, and most of my days I spent in tears from the agony. Eddie Knox and Heather Piercy stuck with me for over two years to get me the help I needed. Due to their efforts the Industrial Commission ruled in my favor and deemed my employer liable for my injury. Due to the delay in my treatment, (seven months) I had to have more extensive surgery and had twice the recovery time than if I had been treated initially. In addition to winning my case and getting me the help I needed, Eddie and Heather supported me emotionally and never waivered in their commitment to me when it felt like the rest of the world was against me. I would recommend The Knox Law Group to anyone. Not only are they the best attorneys anywhere, they are some of the best people I have ever had the privilege to meet.”

-Satisfied Client

I am passionate about workers’ compensation cases because I believe that injured employees deserve protection and justice. I also regularly handle personal injury and other civil litigation matters. I have been with the firm for more than four years, and I work on a team with H. Edward “Eddie” Knox, our managing partner.

Earning my Bachelor of Arts in Journalism and Mass Communication at the University of North Carolina, I have a strong background in writing, editing, and public speaking. After Carolina, I went on to complete my Juris Doctor at Charlotte School of Law, receiving the distinction of cum laude on my law degree. While at Charlotte Law, I was inducted into the Order of the Crown.

I am a native of Denver, North Carolina, but have resided in Charlotte for more than five years. I am committed to serving the community in the Queen City and surrounding areas. I am a member of the North Carolina State Bar, the Mecklenburg County Bar, and the Charlotte Women Attorneys. I am an active volunteer for the annual Fighting For Women with Fashion event to benefit the Clyde and Ethel Dickson domestic violence shelter.

Most importantly, I am dedicated to serving as both an attorney and a true counselor for my clients.

See some of Heather’s client reviews below:

“I felt as though I had known Heather my entire life from our first meeting. She is genuine and caring. She went above and beyond the call of duty for me. I cannot say enough good about her.”

-Satisfied Client

“In March of 2011 I was seriously injured at work. I had the cartilage torn completely out of my left hip socket. The doctors that my employer sent me to were dismissive, rude and unprofessional. They said my injury was pre-existing even though I had no pain prior to the accident, and their own radiologist put in his report that there was no evidence of wear and tear to my hip indicating that it was pre-existing. They put me at maximum medical improvement with no treatment whatsoever and said I was fine to return to my job as a paramedic. I was in tremendous pain. I couldn't sleep, and most of my days I spent in tears from the agony. Eddie Knox and Heather Piercy stuck with me for over two years to get me the help I needed. Due to their efforts the Industrial Commission ruled in my favor and deemed my employer liable for my injury. Due to the delay in my treatment, (seven months) I had to have more extensive surgery and had twice the recovery time than if I had been treated initially. In addition to winning my case and getting me the help I needed, Eddie and Heather supported me emotionally and never waivered in their commitment to me when it felt like the rest of the world was against me. I would recommend The Knox Law Group to anyone. Not only are they the best attorneys anywhere, they are some of the best people I have ever had the privilege to meet.”

-Satisfied Client

attorneys.name: Rebecca J. Pomeroy
attorneys.practice_type: Residential Real Estate Lawyers in Lincolnton, NC
attorneys.bio:
Rebecca’s practice area is focused on residential real estate, probate, and estate planning. Rebecca closes loans for home purchases, refinance and equity lines as well as residential investment properties. Additionally, Rebecca spends time working with family members when a loved one passes away handling their final affairs and settling of estates. She works with many clients on estate planning including preparation of Wills, Financial Powers of Attorney and Healthcare Power of Attorneys as well as Guardianships.

Rebecca grew up in the Lincoln County residing in the Denver area most of her childhood years. She attended East Lincoln High School and completed her high school education at Rocky Mount Academy in Rocky Mount, North Carolina where she met her husband, W. Todd Pomeroy. She attended Salem College in Winston Salem for two years and graduated from the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology. Prior to law school Rebecca worked in Rocky Mount, North Carolina for the Poyner and Spruill Law Firm. Rebecca attended Cumberland School of Law at Samford University in Birmingham, Alabama, graduating in 1996.

In 1996, Rebecca returned to Lincolnton, North Carolina to become a fourth-generation member of the firm and pursue her childhood dream of practicing law with her grandfather, Harvey A. Jonas, Jr. and has remained at the firm for her entire legal career.

Rebecca and her husband, the Honorable W. Todd Pomeroy, became partners with the firm in 2000. Rebecca continues as a partner for the firm and her husband left the firm in 2015 after being appointed as a Superior Court Judge for the 27B Judicial District.

Rebecca has been a member and treasurer for the Lincoln County Bar Association since 1996. Rebecca is also a member of the 27B Bar Association and the North Carolina Bar Association. She is a former member of the Lincolnton Rotary Club, the Downtown Development Program for Lincolnton and the Hospice Board. Rebecca is a former Trustee for First United Methodist Church of Lincolnton where she is a member and was actively involved in setting up the Safe Sanctuary Program for the church. Rebecca is currently the Bar Councilor for the North Carolina State Bar for the 27B district and an outside Board Member with First Federal Savings Bank of Lincolnton.

Rebecca and her husband, Todd, were married in law school and have one child, Elijah Jonas Pomeroy. She enjoys spending time with her family and friends, attending her son’s sporting events, being involved in her son’s school, and time at her second home in Blowing Rock.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Apex, NC
attorneys.bio:
Rebecca A. Poole is a Board-Certified Specialist in Family Law who has practiced exclusively in family law for more than a decade. Rebecca received her Bachelor of Science Degree in Business Administration from Meredith College in 2008 and her Juris Doctor from North Carolina Central University School of Law in 2011.

Prior to opening her own firm, Rebecca practiced family law at three boutique family law firms throughout the triangle area where she gained a wealth of knowledge on representing clients with their family law issues. Rebecca focuses her practice on all aspects of family law, including custody, child support, spousal support, equitable distribution, mediation, negotiations, and collaborative divorces. Rebecca is also certified as a Parenting Coordinator (PC) by the Center for Cooperative Parenting and serves as a PC in high conflict custody cases.

Rebecca is a former Board Member and Co-Secretary for the Center for Cooperative Parenting and has presented at training seminars for those seeking certification as a Parenting Coordinator. She was also selected for inclusion as a "Rising Star" in family law by the publication "North Carolina Super Lawyers".

attorneys.name: Anita R Powers
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Anita R. Powers
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Wallace, NC
attorneys.bio:
Anita R. Powers is a resident of Wallace, North Carolina. She attended Duplin County Schools and graduated from Wallace-Rose Hill High School in 1978. She continued her education at UNC at Charlotte and received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science in May, 1981. She entered North Carolina Central University School of Law in 1981 and graduated in May, 1984 with a Juris Doctorate degree. Her first legal position was as an Assistant District Attorney for the 12th Judicial District, covering Cumberland and Hoke counties. She remained there until she became a partner in the law firm, Baker and Powers, in Lexington, North Carolina in 1986. After eight years, she returned to her hometown and opened her own law practice. She began her practice in Wallace, North Carolina in January 1995 and although she is a general practitioner, her main areas of practice are family law, criminal and traffic law. She has been practicing law for over thirty-five years. In her business she has helped countless clients with their legal issues, some, on a pro bono basis.

Ms. Powers has been involved in various organizations and committees. She is currently serving in her third term as Chair of the Board of Trustees for James Sprunt Community College and as a member of the Duplin County Elections Board. She previously served on the N. C. State Board of Community Colleges and as an elected official on the Duplin County Board of Commissioners, representing District 5. She volunteers as a Judge with the Duplin County Teen Court, is a life member of the Duplin County Branch of the NAACP, a Diamond Life Member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc., Duplin County Alumnae Chapter and served as Chair of the Regional Nominating Committee for the South Atlantic Region covering NC, SC, VA and Bermuda (2011-2014). She is a past Board Member of Duplin County Economic Development and the Eastpointe County Commissioner Advisory Committee.

Ms. Powers has been a presenter at churches and organizations on various legal and social issues.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Wilson, NC
attorneys.bio:
J. Chris Price is a dedicated and experienced attorney with a broad range of expertise in civil litigation, complex property issues, traffic offenses, DWI defense, and estate planning. With a proven track record of representing clients in a variety of legal matters, Chris is committed to providing clear, effective, and compassionate legal guidance.

Outside of his legal practice, Chris is a proud father to three children—Ethan, Ashby, and Bodie—and is married to his beautiful wife, Elizabeth. He balances his professional life with his passion for family and outdoor activities, including coaching his oldest son in competitive wakeboarding and enjoying camping trips with his family.

Chris currently serves as the 1st Vice President of the Eighth Judicial District Bar and as a board member for the Wilson Chamber of Commerce. He brings his leadership experience and a commitment to service into his role, always striving to make a positive impact on both the legal community and the wider public.

In addition to his legal career, Chris has an extensive background in public service. He is a former Senior Firefighter with the City of Rocky Mount, a Fire Inspector for the Town of Apex, and has served as a firefighter with the Rock Ridge Volunteer Fire Department. This experience has helped shape his strong work ethic, sense of duty, and deep understanding of the importance of service to others.

Whether navigating complex legal issues or helping clients plan for the future, J. Chris Price is a trusted advocate with the skills and dedication to handle a wide range of legal matters while balancing a fulfilling personal life and commitment to community service.

Jessica will explore all available options and guide her clients through these difficult decisions. She will utilize her sharp legal savvy and experience as a parent for the benefit of her clients and is a great asset to all those whom she serves.

attorneys.name: Cindi M. Quay
attorneys.practice_type: Powers of Attorney and Appointment Lawyers in New Bern, NC
attorneys.bio:
Cindi M. Quay joined the United States Marine Corps out of High School and received an Honorable Discharge in 1987. She obtained a B.A. in Justice and Public Policy at North Carolina Wesleyan College at Rocky Mount in 1994. After working as a paralegal for several years, she decided to attend law school at North Carolina Central University in 1997. Cindi was admitted to the North Carolina bar in 2000.

From 2000 to 2006, Cindi was employed as an Associate Attorney at Ward and Smith, P.A. in New Bern, N.C. During her employment with Ward and Smith she practiced in the areas of general litigation, employment law and family law. In 2006, she opened her own practice in New Bern, N.C. She built her practice focusing primarily on family law, estate planning and estate administration. In 2012, Cindi expanded her firm, hired an Associate Attorney, and changed the firm name to Quay & Associates, P.A.

In October 2012, Cindi was appointed Public Administrator for Craven County, North Carolina. Her role as a Public Administrator has further expanded into Pamlico County. Cindi's practice is now focused in the areas of Estate Administration, Estate Planning, Guardianship, and Elder Law.

In addition to her Estate practice, Cindi has been the Attorney Advocate for the Judicial District 3B Guardian ad Litem Program since 2017. She represents children in Carteret, Craven, and Pamlico Counties who have been displaced from their parents due to abuse or neglect.

attorneys.name: Christopher P. Raab
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Chris is a Shareholder at Caudle & Spears. His practice focuses on business litigation, appellate litigation, and employment law. Chris is licensed in North Carolina and South Carolina.

Chris advocates for clients in both state and federal court, and he regularly represents clients before the North Carolina appellate courts. He is experienced in all aspects of the litigation process, from commencement of suit through appeal, and has tried multiple cases to jury verdict, including in the North Carolina District and Superior Courts, the North Carolina Business Court, and the United States District Court for the Western District of North Carolina. Chris also frequently represents clients in binding arbitration proceedings.

Chris represents a range of clients including businesses, insurance companies, municipalities, and individuals. He assists clients in cases dealing with:

Covenants not to compete or solicit;

Business torts such as breach of contract, tortious interference, fraud, misappropriation of trade secrets, and unfair and deceptive trade practices;

Executive compensation;

Breach of fiduciary duty and corporate governance issues;

Disputes between shareholders or LLC members;

Automobile dealership law;

Defense of municipalities and their employees against federal civil rights claims; and

Defense of businesses against employment discrimination and wage and hour claims.

In addition to his litigation practice, Chris also advises businesses on human resources and employment law matters, and he represents executives and professionals in negotiating employment and separation agreements.

Chris possesses an AV Preeminent® Peer Review Rating from Martindale-Hubbell, which is given to attorneys who are ranked at the highest level of professional excellence for their legal expertise, communication skills, and ethical standards by their peers. For each of the past nine years, Chris has also been recognized by North Carolina Super Lawyers magazine as a Rising Star among North Carolina litigators.

attorneys.name: Russell M. Racine
attorneys.practice_type: Aviation Law Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Russell M. Racine joined Dean Gibson Hofer & Nance, PLLC in February 2012. His practice focuses primarily on general civil litigation and insurance defense. Russ is a member of the North Carolina, South Carolina, and Colorado Bar associations. He is also licensed to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

Originally from Spartanburg, South Carolina, Russ attended Muhlenburg College in Allentown, Pennsylvania. After graduating with a Bachelor of Science in Chemistry and Natural Science, he worked as a chemist for three years before attending law school. In 1999, Russ received his J.D. from the University of Denver College of Law, in Denver, Colorado. While in law school, he was a member of the moot court team and clerked for an intellectual property law firm.

Following graduation, Russ worked as an assistant solicitor in Spartanburg, South Carolina, for three years. During that time, he conducted numerous felony and misdemeanor jury trials, negotiated and presented guilty pleas, and participated in the development of Drug Court.

Russ relocated to Charlotte, North Carolina, in 2004. For the next seven years, he devoted his practice to intellectual property and business litigation. As part of that practice, he represented clients in litigations in multiple jurisdictions including North Carolina, South Carolina, New York, California, and Texas. His litigations also included representing businesses in opposition and cancellation proceedings before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board and Internet domain disputes before the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers. Russ also counseled clients regarding protection of intellectual property, and drafted and prosecuted patent applications at the United States Patent and Trademark Office. Additionally, he has litigated home construction defects, business matters, including unfair and deceptive trade practices, South Carolina lemon law violations, and personal injury cases involving motor vehicles and construction accidents.

Russ is a Certified DRC Mediator and conducts Superior Court mediation settlement conferences for all types of cases.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Dedicated Family Law & Estate Planning Attorney

With a passion for helping families through life's most challenging transitions, I bring nearly a decade of diverse legal experience to serve my clients with compassion, skill, and dedication. As the daughter of a U.S. Army Soldier and the eldest of four siblings, I grew up moving every three years across the United States and abroad, giving me a unique perspective on family dynamics and the challenges of transitions.

sections.title: Education
content: I earned my Juris Doctor from Campbell University School of Law in 2017, where I honed my advocacy skills through Moot Court, the Kilpatrick Mock Trial Competition, and as a Negotiation Competitor. My foundation in creative thinking began with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Creative Writing from the University of North Carolina Wilmington.

After being licensed to practice law in North Carolina in 2017, I began my career at King Law Offices, PLLC, where I quickly advanced to Junior Partner. There, I developed a diverse practice handling estate planning, family law, civil matters, and criminal defense throughout western North Carolina.

In April 2021, I joined Bull & Reinhardt, PLLC, focusing my practice on family law, estate planning, and estate administration, helping clients navigate complex personal and financial transitions with clarity and compassion.

From June 2023 to March 2025, I served at the Cumberland County District Attorney's Office, prosecuting crimes involving domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking. This experience deepened my understanding of the profound impact these issues have on families and communities, while strengthening my courtroom advocacy skills.

I am thrilled to have returned to Bull & Reinhardt in March 2025, where I continue to help clients with family law matters, estate planning, estate administration, traffic matters, misdemeanor charges, and domestic assault cases.
My practice focuses on guiding clients through life's most significant challenges and transitions:
Family Law: Divorce, child custody, support matters, domestic violence protection
Estate Planning: Wills, trusts, powers of attorney, advance directives
Estate Administration: Probate, asset distribution, executor assistance
Traffic: Traffic violations and related legal matters
Misdemeanor Charges: Defense for a variety of misdemeanor criminal offenses
Domestic Assaults: Legal representation in domestic assault cases
I believe in giving back to our community. My service includes:
Girl Scouts Gold Award recipient (equivalent to Eagle Scout) with over 80 hours of community service
Volunteer with Wills for Heroes program
Pro Bono work through 4ALL in Western North Carolina
Why Choose Me As Your Attorney

I understand that legal issues involving your family or future planning are deeply personal. My background in creative writing, coupled with extensive courtroom experience in both family law and criminal prosecution, allows me to approach each case with a unique blend of compassion, creativity, and strategic advocacy.

I take pride in treating each client with the dignity and respect that all human beings deserve. Having experienced frequent relocations during my military family upbringing, I understand the importance of stability and clear guidance during periods of change. I strive to meet people where they are in life and equip them with the knowledge needed to navigate the legal system with confidence.
My commitment is to make complex legal matters accessible to my clients, ensuring you understand your options and can make informed decisions during challenging times.

attorneys.name: Neal Andrew Ramee
attorneys.practice_type: Education Law Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Neal Ramee is a partner in the firm's Education Section. He received his undergraduate degree in philosophy from the University of Virginia and his law degree from the University of North Carolina School of Law, where he was inducted into the Order of the Coif. While in law school, Mr. Ramee served as Managing Editor of the First Amendment Law Review and as an Honors Writing Scholar. Before joining the firm in 2005, he served for two years as a law clerk to Justice Mark Martin at the North Carolina Supreme Court.

Mr. Ramee has litigated cases in state and federal court involving the First Amendment, contract and employment disputes, student assignment, the Fair Labor Standards Act, negligence claims, and federal civil rights issues, among other matters. He has published articles and delivered presentations to school officials and school attorneys on diverse topics including the First Amendment, student assignment, cyber-bullying, child custody, student records, internal investigations, and the use of public-private partnerships for school construction. He has also taught a class in legal reasoning and writing as an adjunct faculty member at the University of North Carolina School of Law.

Mr. Ramee has served as Secretary/Treasurer of the Education Section of the North Carolina Bar Association and as editor of its publication, Education Law. He is a member of the North Carolina Council of School Attorneys, the National Council of School Attorneys, and the American Immigration Law Association. Mr. Ramee is licensed in North Carolina and has been admitted to practice before the federal courts in the Eastern and Middle Districts of North Carolina. His practice is dedicated to representation of public schools and other educational institutions, with a particular focus on the state and federal constitutions, appellate practice, student discipline, student assignment, and immigration issues arising in the public school context.

attorneys.name: Danielle N. Randolph
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Administration Lawyers in Lincolnton, NC
attorneys.bio:
Danielle Randolph is a committed and client-focused attorney who proudly serves clients in a wide range of estate planning and estate administration matters. Her practice includes the preparation of wills, living wills, trusts, powers of attorney, healthcare powers of attorney, and both intestate and testate estate administration. While estate planning is her primary focus, she also assists clients with family law matters, including divorce, child custody, child support, post-separation support, alimony, and domestic violence.

Born and raised in Lincolnton, North Carolina, Danielle brings a strong connection to the community she serves. After graduating from Lincolnton High School, Danielle obtained her Bachelors of Business Administration, cum laude in Trust and Wealth Management from Campbell University and was awarded a Trust Certificate, further strengthening her ability to assist clients with estate planning and asset protection. She then received a Academic Merit Scholarship to Charleston School of Law. During law school, Danielle participated in an externship with Charleston Pro Bono Legal Services assisting low income individuals dealing with evictions. Upon graduating and obtaining her Juris Doctor, Danielle was sworn into the North Carolina State Bar in April 2025. Thereafter, she began working for The Pendleton Law Firm where she has been practicing since.

The Pendleton Law Firm takes a team approach when assisting clients. Danielle and Clay Pendleton, who has over 35 years of experience, work closely together to strategize and obtain the best outcome for their clients. While working closely with Clay, Danielle has gained valuable insight and mentorship that strengthens her advocacy and strategic approach in their cases. Along with the attorneys, Kaitlyn, Holly, and Janel are the support system behind the family law and estate planning division.

Outside the office, Danielle enjoys spending quality time with her fiancé and their two doodles, embracing the balance between a fulfilling professional life and meaningful personal moments.

attorneys.name: Eben T. Rawls III
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
An attorney with more than 30 years’ experience, Eben T. Rawls III has represented many professionals, doctors, lawyers, bankers, securities traders, CEO’s, labor union presidents and elected officials. Mr. Rawls focuses exclusively on defending people accused of crimes at his Charlotte firm, Rawls, Scheer, Clary, Mingo, P.L.L.C .He is also board certified by the North Carolina State Bar as a specialist in the areas of federal criminal law and North Carolina state criminal law.

Mr. Rawls has handled cases in North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Virginia, New York, New Jersey and California. He has also handled complicated international cases that required travel to Norway, England and other foreign nations. He has received an AV* rating by Martindale-Hubbell signifying the highest legal ability rating and the highest rating for ethical conduct. The Bar Registry of Preeminent Lawyers lists Mr. Rawls as one of the nation’s top criminal defense attorneys.

Mr. Rawls is admitted to practice in North Carolina and the Eastern, Western and Middle Districts of the U.S. District Courts of North Carolina, as well as the U.S. Supreme Court.

Eben Rawls is an accomplished lawyer and advocate with a highly successful track record of resolving difficult criminal matters in State and Federal courts. Once Mr. Rawls agrees to represent you, he is personally responsible for your case. He has extremely talented and experienced staff, most of whom have been with him longer than 10 years, and who know how to get things done.

Mr. Rawls has worked with and utilizes a number of experienced and well-respected experts to assist him and his clients. These include experienced investigators who formerly worked in federal and state law enforcement, forensic accountants, acoustic experts, computer and technology experts, DNA experts, cell tower experts, forensic psychologists and psychiatrists, and many others. Once Mr. Rawls becomes involved in the client’s case, he recognizes the importance of being able to interview witnesses quickly and thoroughly, obtain information relevant and needed to convince the Prosecution to decline prosecution or drop charges. If charges are not declined or dropped, the quick gathering of information and involvement of experts seriously mitigates the case.

Mr. Rawls has represented numerous individuals and corporations that have been investigated or prosecuted for alleged Federal crimes including: tax evasion, fraud, public corruption, obstruction of justice, drug violations, firearms violations, securities violations, money laundering, pornography, environmental offenses, and many others.

Mr. Rawls has represented numerous individuals investigated or prosecuted in State courts for alleged state crimes including: numerous homicide cases, assaults, drug cases, embezzlement, fraud, and many other serious felonies and misdemeanors.

Mr. Rawls has represented numerous attorneys, medical professionals, financially licensed professionals, professional athletes, business owners, public officials, law enforcement personnel, and high-ranking officers in corporations, to name but a few. Because of the sensitivity of most of his matters, Mr. Rawls strives to keep the names and matters of his clients out of the public press and media.

He taught 7th grade science in Louisville, Kentucky for two years, during which time he earned a master's degree from the University of Louisville. attorneys.name: Jennifer R. Reed
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Mooresville, NC
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer R. Reed is an associate attorney at Grimes Yeoman, PLLC. She obtained her bachelor’s degree from Messiah College in 2012 and her law degree from Penn State University, The Dickinson School of Law in 2015. Ms. Reed was a member of the Public Interest Law Fund, a volunteer supervisor for the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program, and a senior editor of the Yearbook on Arbitration and Mediation. Her article, South Africa Revolutionizing Foreign Investment Protections was published in the 2014 edition of the Yearbook. Additionally, she interned for MidPenn Legal Services and The Honorable Richard A. Lewis, President Judge of the Dauphin County Court of Common Pleas. She received a CALI Award in 2014 for achieving the highest grade in her Disability Law class.

Following graduation, Ms. Reed was a law clerk for the Honorable Edward E. Guido, President Judge of the Cumberland County Court of Common Pleas. As a law clerk, she drafted judicial opinions in civil and criminal matters and assisted with drafting local rules of court. In 2016, she coordinated programming for Cumberland County’s Law Day and volunteered with Will for Heroes to provide essential legal documents for first responders. Following her clerkship, Ms. Reed worked as a staff attorney for MidPenn Legal Services. She began by representing tenants in housing matters and coordinating legal clinics at homeless shelters and then transitioned to a grant-funded position representing victims of domestic and sexual violence in family and civil matters. After relocating from Pennsylvania to North Carolina, Ms. Reed took the North Carolina bar exam to obtain North Carolina licensure and worked as a document review attorney.

Ms. Reed is licensed to practice law in North Carolina and Pennsylvania.

attorneys.name: Katlyn A. Reh
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Katlyn A. Reh, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
** Serving clients throughout Mecklenburg County **

From the time I was a young girl, I always dreamed of opening my own business. My desire to learn more about business led me to attend Manhattan College for undergraduate school, where I majored in Finance and Managerial Science with a minor in Marketing. In college, I discovered my fascination with the law and realized that I wanted to build a career where I could work with clients directly and have the opportunity to help people when they need it most. I graduated from the school of business with my bachelor's degree one year early, and I immediately went on to earn my Juris Doctor degree from the University of Miami School of Law. I am licensed to practice law in both Texas and North Carolina, and I have practiced family law in both states.

I approach family law from a non-judgmental place, where I put myself in my client's shoes and work with my clients to help them achieve the life that they desire. It is my mission to build trust with clients, have open lines of communication and to help people in my local community navigate through the complexities of the legal system. I am also deeply passionate about children's rights, and I am a Custody Advocate with the Council for Children's Rights and a Guardian ad Litem to children in the foster care system. In my free time, I enjoy reading, writing, playing tennis, and trying different restaurants. I always welcome a new culinary recommendation!

Opening my own solo practice is a dream come true and I am overjoyed to be able to combine my love of business with my love of family law. I appreciate you taking the time to read about me, and I encourage you to reach out so that I can have the opportunity to learn more about you. Regardless of what family law issue you may be dealing with, let's touch base. I look forward to hearing from you.

attorneys.bio:
Senta F. Rhodes is an experienced trial attorney who is admitted to practice law in 3 states including North Carolina, The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and The State of Maryland. attorneys.name: Johnathan L. Rhyne Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lincolnton, NC
attorneys.bio:
Practicing family law is a 24/7 undertaking. While other areas of the law are static, in family law there is something happening all the time — the parties’ business is either increasing or decreasing in value, the other parent is late bringing the child home, the client is having trouble with the emotions of it all, the bills are not being paid, an argument just broke out. Those ever-changing dynamics are what makes practicing family law such a challenge. Fortunately, those challenges can be overcome by an attorney with the right blend of experience, training, patience and plain old hard work. That’s what I bring to the table for all my clients and that’s why people hire me to manage their family issues.

For 39 years, the past 26 as a Board Certified Family Law Specialist, I have dedicated my practice to helping families cope with what they never thought they would confront - separation and divorce, disagreements over custody, and family financial issues. Fortunately, over my career I have seen it all and helped clients through it all. Knowing that I have helped many before them seems to comfort new clients. Often just knowing that we have the capability to help is the thing of most value.

One important thing that I’ve learned over my career is that an able and experienced staff is essential. I have the best. Rebecca Yoder is my partner and right hand, and is also certified by the North Carolina State Bar as a specialist in family law. She now has nine years of practice under her belt and couples that experience with a keen intellect. She is a very fine lawyer and our clients love her.

My clients love my two paralegals. Bobbie Little joined the firm as a high school student. More than 30 years later, she has the optimal blend of patience and experience. Brandi Ballard rounds out our team. Brandi has high energy and puts her 20 years with the firm to great use every day.

Mr. Rhyne graduated from Davidson College with a B.A. and Campbell University School of Law with a J.D. He is a former member of the North Carolina General Assembly.

Aside from his family and law practice, his passion is Davidson College basketball. Go Cats!

His approach is to provide his clients complete access to him for any counsel or insight they may need, keeping them informed and up to date on their case every step of the way.

Standing up for the rights of the injured is what Brian does. From insurance companies to employers to corporations, no fight is too big for him to take on.

attorneys.name: Donna Ambler Rice Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Chapel Hill, NC
attorneys.bio:
Donna Ambler Rice received her B.A. degree, magna cum laude, from Montclair State College in May 1985 and her Juris Doctor degree from Washington & Lee University School of Law in May 1988. She is the past Chairperson of the Children's Issue Committee of the Family Law Section of the North Carolina Bar Association, the past Chairperson of the Orange County Family Lawyer's Association, the past Secretary/Treasurer and the past President of the Judicial District 18 Bar Association and the former Chairperson of the North Carolina Academy of Trial Lawyer's Family Law Section. She is currently a member of the North Carolina State Bar, the North Carolina Bar Association and its Family Law Section, the Judicial District 18 Bar Association, the Orange County Bar Association, the North Carolina Advocates of Justice, the Academy of Family Mediators, and the Triangle Collaborative Family Law Association.

Donna Ambler Rice has also successfully advocated for her clients before the North Carolina Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of North Carolina in the following cases:

In the Matter of the Adoption of P.E.P., 407 S.E.2d 505, 329 N.C. 692 (N.C., 1991) - The Supreme Court held that violations by adoptive parents and their attorney of statute prohibiting any fee or compensation for placing or arranging adoption of child, together with numerous other irregularities in adoption case, invalidated adoption proceeding; and

Petersen v. Rogers, 445 S.E.2d 901, 337 N.C. 397 (N.C., 1994) - The Supreme Court held that (1) natural parents' constitutionally protected paramount right to custody, care and control of their child outweighed interests of a married couple seeking to adopt the child, and (2) a married couple seeking to adopt the child had no right to visitation or to file action requesting visitation period.

Donna Ambler Rice has a true passion for being a family law attorney and describes her career as follows:

"For me, being a family law attorney is not just a job; it is who I am. I think about cases in the middle of the night. I am often jumping out of the shower to jot down a note about a client's case. The reward for me is seeing people become their best selves. It's a long road, but I enjoy helping people rebuild their lives; helping them find a place of stability and health. Whether it's mediation, litigation, or some combination, we are as creative as possible - working for our clients' best interest and to guide them a place of wholeness."

attorneys.name: Alex Riddle
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Goldsboro, NC
attorneys.bio:
Alex Riddle joined Riddle & Riddle Injury Lawyers in 2020 as a personal injury lawyer handling all types of injury cases throughout North Carolina. She graduated from the University of North Carolina School of Law in 2020 and joined the firm immediately after passing the North Carolina State Bar. She is particularly interested in civil rights law.

Prior to attending law school, Alex earned her B.A. degree in History from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, graduating with Distinction.

A Passion for Justice

Alex is a passionate advocate for justice for all. Before joining the firm, Alex volunteered for the Innocence Project, helping find ways for those who maintain their innocence to appeal their cases. She has also worked for an immigration law clinic, and has significant experience working with Spanish-speaking clients and interpreters.

She previously clerked for Judge Allen Baddour in Superior Court.

A Legacy in Law

Alex is the daughter of founding attorney and managing partner Gene Riddle and a native of Goldsboro, North Carolina.

"Growing up I watched my dad practice law. I loved seeing the great impact he had on our community. I am excited to serve the community that I grew up in."

-Alex Riddle, attorney

In 2021, Alex was named a member in The National Trial Lawyers Top 40 Under 40.

Other Interests

When she's not advocating on behalf of injured North Carolinians, Alex enjoys barre, cycling, and anything related to UNC basketball. Alex also has a beloved dog, Roscoe, that she rescued as a sophomore in high school.

attorneys.name: Dean Riddle
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Litigation Lawyers in Goldsboro, NC
attorneys.bio:
Dean A. Riddle is a founding shareholder of Riddle & Williams, P.C. Alongside his brother, Gene Riddle, Dean also leads Riddle & Riddle’s insurance litigation department. For nearly 40 years, Dean has concentrated his practice on insurance claims, community association law, and commercial litigation. At Riddle & Riddle Injury Lawyers, he is especially focused on helping victims of natural disasters like Hurricane Helene get the compensation they deserve.

Dean’s litigation experience is substantial and diverse in both state and federal courts, and includes handling cases involving bad faith insurance practices, construction defect claims, contested/wrongful foreclosures, contract disputes, wrongful death, and employment discrimination. He is a member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, which is a prestigious group of trial lawyers limited to attorneys who have won multi-million dollar verdicts, awards, and settlements. He is AV Preeminent® rated by Martindale-Hubbell®, the highest rating an attorney can receive.

“I’m committed to helping victims get maximum compensation from insurance companies.”

-Dean Riddle, attorney, Riddle & Riddle Injury Lawyers

A Reputation for Success

Since 1985, Dean Riddle has earned a reputation for securing maximum compensation in insurance disputes. In 2024, for example, he secured over $1,000,000 in an insurance dispute involving a fire at an apartment complex.

Dean views his work fighting for victims as a personal mission, inspired by the values instilled in him by his father. His father, Dr. Gene Riddle, encouraged both Dean and his brother, Gene, to pursue careers in law.

attorneys.name: J. Michael Riley
attorneys.practice_type: Asbestos Mesothelioma Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Mike has been practicing law with Martin & Jones for more than 20 years and his practice focuses on representing individuals suffering from asbestos-related diseases including malignant mesothelioma, asbestos related lung cancer and asbestosis. His clients include workers who were occupationally exposed to asbestos in industrial settings such as power plants, chemical plants, railroads, shipyards, paper mills and other manufacturing facilities. Mike has represented clients from states all over the United States as well as from various provinces in Canada.

The cases have included products liability and wrongful death actions in federal court and various state courts, and workers compensation occupational disease claims before the North Carolina Industrial Commission. The defendants have included asbestos manufacturers, contractors, distributors and employers.

Mike has achieved the highest attorney rating, "AV," by Martindale-Hubbell, an independent legal services company whose peer-review attorney ratings service is an objective indicator that an attorney has the highest ethical standards and professional ability. He graduated from the University of North Carolina School of Law after graduating from Wake Forest University with a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics.

Mike pursues claims on behalf of clients against various asbestos company bankruptcy administrative claims trusts, and also serves as an arbitrator and member of the trust advisory committee with different trusts.

He lives in Raleigh with his wife and enjoys watching and participating in sports as well as playing music in his band.

attorneys.name: James M. Roane III
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Neglect Lawyers in Greensboro, NC
attorneys.bio:
James Roane is the owner and lead attorney of Roane Law in Greensboro, NC, a successful

law firm representing plaintiffs in legal proceedings involving serious motor vehicle and

personal injury accidents as well as nursing home neglect and abuse cases. He has been

practicing in North Carolina since 1999, and is a member of the North Carolina Bar Association,

the North Carolina Advocates for Justice, the American Association for Justice, the Inns of Court

and the Friends of Residents in Long Term Care.

James graduated Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science from the

University of North Carolina at Greensboro in 1992. During his undergraduate years, James was

a two-term president of Tau Kappa Epsilon and worked as a supervisor at UPS. He went on to

earn his J.D. in 1999 from the Wake Forest University School of Law in Winston-Salem, NC.

During this time, James earned several honors including Most Outstanding Advocate from the

North Carolina Academy of Trial Lawyers, was a regional winner on the National Trial Team as

well as the Elite Eight in the National Competition.

A few years after graduating from law school, James accepted a position as Director of

Litigation with Crumley & Associates, the largest consumer-based law firm in North Carolina.

During his tenure at Crumley & Associates, James led a team of four attorneys and five

paralegals as supervising attorney. He left Crumley & Associates in April 2008 to pursue his

dream of opening his own firm.

In addition to running a successful law firm, James currently serves as Adjunct Trial

Practice Professor at the Elon University School of Law in Greensboro. His responsibilities in

this role include instruction of foundational trial skills and advocacy to law students ... a role he

finds fulfilling and one which challenges him to continually seek new approaches to this craft.

Another role in which James was able to provide professional guidance was as a member

of the Search Committee for a new dean for the Wake Forest School of Law. In March 2007, his

input as a graduate and as a practicing legal professional helped the committee find a new dean

to guide the law school into the future.

In every endeavor undertaken, James has thrived and has been widely recognized for his

efforts. As mentioned above, he was named Most Outstanding Advocate by the North Carolina

Academy of Trial Lawyers while in law school; Legal Elite 2007 named him top attorney in

North Carolina under the age of 40 after he was chosen by a poll of almost 18,000 licensed

attorneys who read BUSINESS North Carolina Magazine; and in 2008, the North Carolina

Advocates of Justice awarded him their coveted Order of Service Award.

Professionally, James remains active in publishing and speaking. His verdicts have been

published several times in Lawyers Weekly, and he has been featured in local newspapers. James

is a popular and charismatic speaker, and as the current Vice President of the Nursing Home

Division of the North Carolina Advocates of Justice and a member of the Guilford County

Nursing Home Advisory Committee, James speaks to groups on such topics as disaster

preparedness for nursing homes, the arbitration of a nursing home case, expert witness rules and

special considerations in nursing home cases, and basic nursing home negligence.

James is married to Sarah Roane, also a practicing attorney. In addition to being a

devoted husband and father, James enjoys recreational volleyball, bicycling and coastal fishing.

attorneys.name: A. Patrick Roberts
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
North Carolina Criminal Defense Attorney

When you or someone you love is facing serious criminal charges, the fear is immediate and overwhelming. Your reputation, freedom, career, and family may all feel at risk — and the legal system can feel confusing, unforgiving, and stacked against you.

Patrick Roberts understands that fear. For more than two decades, he has stood beside people at their most vulnerable moments and guided them through some of the most serious criminal cases in North Carolina.

Patrick Roberts is the founder of Patrick Roberts Law PLLC and a veteran criminal defense attorney with over 21 years of courtroom experience. He has handled thousands of criminal cases across North Carolina, including high-stakes felony matters involving sex crime allegations, child sexual assault accusations, drug trafficking, domestic violence, and complex white-collar charges.

What sets Patrick Roberts apart is not just experience — it’s perspective.

Before dedicating his career to defending the accused, Mr. Roberts served as an Assistant County Attorney in three North Carolina jurisdictions. He knows how prosecutors evaluate cases, where investigations break down, and how charging decisions are really made behind closed doors. That insider understanding allows him to identify weaknesses early and protect clients long before trial becomes inevitable.

Clients and families often come to Mr. Roberts feeling panicked, ashamed, or unsure who to trust. His approach is calm, direct, and strategic. He takes the time to explain what is happening, what is likely to happen next, and — most importantly — what can be done to protect the client’s future. Many cases are resolved quietly and favorably because of decisions made before charges are ever filed.

Mr. Roberts is a seasoned trial lawyer, but he is equally known for preventing cases from escalating unnecessarily. When trial is unavoidable, he brings disciplined preparation, sharp cross-examination, and a deep understanding of North Carolina criminal procedure into the courtroom.

His professional credentials reflect the respect he has earned within the legal community:

→ Graduate of Duke University School of Law

→ Bachelor’s degree from The Johns Hopkins University

→ AV Preeminent® rating from Martindale-Hubbell (peer-reviewed)

→ Featured in Super Lawyers Magazine

→ Featured on the cover of Attorney-at-Law Magazine

→ Quoted by national outlets including USA Today and Fox News

→ Co-author of two legal books

→ Former Commissioner of the North Carolina State Ethics Commission

→ Former member of the North Carolina Juvenile Justice Planning Committee

→ Admitted to practice in all North Carolina state and federal courts, as well as the United States Supreme Court

Despite these credentials, clients consistently describe Mr. Roberts as approachable, focused, and relentlessly prepared. He understands that no two cases — and no two families — are the same. Every defense strategy is built around the specific facts, risks, and long-term consequences involved.

If you are searching late at night, worried about what tomorrow will bring, know this: an accusation is not a conviction. There are options. There are defenses. And having the right attorney early can change everything.

Patrick Roberts does not promise outcomes — no ethical lawyer can. What he does promise is experience, honesty, preparation, and an unwavering commitment to protecting his clients at every stage of the criminal process.

Larry's practice areas include estate planning and charitable giving, elder law, planning for children and adults with special needs, business organizations and tax law and estate and trust administration.

attorneys.name: Randall M. Roden
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Randall Roden is a trial and appellate lawyer who began his career with the United States Department of Justice. During his more than six years with the Justice Department, he tried cases in federal courts throughout the Southeast. He now handles civil trials and appeals at all levels in the state and federal court systems in North Carolina, primarily representing individuals and businesses in intellectual property, contract and business ownership disputes.

At Tharrington Smith, Mr. Roden has successfully represented both plaintiffs and defendants. He is listed in Best Lawyers In America®, 2013 & 2014 for distinction in intellectual property litigation. Although the majority of his cases involve intellectual property or other business disputes, he also has extensive experience in media and First Amendment cases, construction litigation, will and estate contests and personal injury litigation.

Mr. Roden has been appointed by the Chief Judge of the Eastern District of North Carolina to a second two-year term on the Civil Rules Subcommittee of the Eastern District of North Carolina.

He is licensed to practice law in North Carolina and the District of Columbia and is a member of the bar of all federal courts in North Carolina, the United States Courts of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit and the District of Columbia Circuit, the United States Claims Court, the United States Tax Court and the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Roden is a member of the American Bar Association (litigation section), the North Carolina Bar Association (litigation section), the Wake County Bar Association and the North Carolina Advocates for Justice.

Mr. Roden grew up in Midland, Texas, and Columbia, Missouri; graduated from Phillips Academy in Andover, Massachusetts in 1964, and from the University of North Carolina with a degree in English in 1973 and a J.D. in 1976; and served in the United States Army from 1966 to 1969. Mr. Roden lives in Chapel Hill, where he has served on the Board of the UNC Institute for the Arts and Humanities, the Chapel Hill Historical Society and is active in other Orange County community organizations.

attorneys.name: Mary Leazer Rogers
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Mary Leazer Rogers
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
If you are facing a state or federal criminal charge, you want a defense lawyer who will give you the time and attention you need to achieve the best possible outcome. At the Law Office of Mary Leazer Rogers in Charlotte, North Carolina, we will listen to you, provide you with an honest assessment of your case, and advocate aggressively and relentlessly on your behalf. Our firm represents clients who are under criminal investigation or have been charged with DWI, drug crimes, traffic violations, probation violations, robbery, theft, larceny, weapons violations, assault, and violent crimes.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of James Scott Farrin
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Durham, NC
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Rouse joined the Law Offices of James Scott Farrin in 2010 and handles Social Security Disability claims for our clients.

Ms. Rouse received her J.D. from the North Carolina Central University School of Law and her B.A. in English from Barton College. She has eight years of experience as a Social Security Disability Determination Services Examiner prior to obtaining her law degree in 2008. In addition to Social Security law, Ms. Rouse has practiced in the areas of debtor/creditor mediation, domestic violence and employment securities law.

"I can't tell you how many times people have told me how much anxiety they had about the hearing process," Ms. Rouse said. "Afterwards, they thanked me for making the process more tolerable. Going to a hearing may never be a pleasant experience, but at least I was able to make it more palatable for them."

Ms. Rouse is a member of the North Carolina State Bar, the North Carolina Bar Association, the North Carolina Advocates for Justice, the Wake County Bar Association, and the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives. She is the current co-chair of the North Carolina Advocates for Justice CLE Committee. She presented “The Interaction of Social Security Disability and Unemployment Insurance Benefits in NC” at the North Carolina Advocates for Justice CLE on March 30, 2012.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Rousseaux
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Assisting Medical Malpractice Victims in Charlotte

Michael was born in Madrid, Spain where he lived the first five years of his life. Following this, he lived in France, Canada, Pennsylvania, Illinois, North Carolina and Florida. He attended college and law school in North Carolina, and upon graduating in 1990 from the Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law, he got married and decided to establish his personal and professional roots in the Charlotte Metro area.

Michael recalls first being drawn to the legal field when he participated in a mock trial in the sixth grade. As a teenager he became involved with the Boy Scouts of America’s Exploring Program which allowed him to learn more about the field of law through meeting members of the legal community. While studying accounting in college, he had his eyes set on law school the entire time. During Michael’s last year in law school, his father suffered the loss of an eye as a result of a medical error. Seeing firsthand the devastation that can result from medical malpractice became the catalyst for Michael’s career.

The first three years of his career were spent with a general practice firm, learning how to be an attorney, and being exposed to many different areas of practice. The next eight years he worked as insurance defense attorney learning how to be a trial attorney. Since 2002, Michael has leveraged his experience as a defense attorney and combined that with his passion for representing injured people, whether those injuries were caused by medical negligence like his father or motor vehicle negligence.

For the last 18 years, Michael has lived in Weddington, NC with his wife Cathy. Together they have two daughters, Alex and Maddy. He is a member of Carmel Baptist Church and an avid tennis player as a member of multiple USTA and Queen City teams.

At our firm, we are family and will treat you like family. Our team of Charlotte personal injury attorneys can ensure that you are well taken care of. Contact us today to learn more about how we can help!
