attorneys.name: Alice Stubbs
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Alice C. Stubbs is a partner in the firm. She joined Tharrington Smith in 2006 after completing eight years as a Wake County District Court judge. First appointed in 1997 by Governor Jim Hunt, she was elected to the judgeship in 1998 and 2002. During her time on the bench, Ms. Stubbs presided in domestic court; was certified as a juvenile judge in 2001; and was designated as a family court judge from 2002 through 2005.

Ms. Stubbs is a native of New Bern. She graduated from Phillips Academy in Andover, Massachusetts in 1985, from Davidson College in 1989 with a major in economics, attended University College in London, and received her law degree from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1992. She then clerked for Chief Judge James B. Wolfe, Jr., of the United States Bankruptcy Court in the Middle District of North Carolina, followed by a litigation practice with Stubbs and Perdue, P.A.

Long active in bar association activities, Ms. Stubbs has served on the Board of Directors for the Wake County Bar Association. In 2008, she served as the vice chairman of the Continuing Legal Education Committee for the Wake County Bar Association. She is a member of the Family Law Section of the North Carolina Bar Association. She has served on the Litigation Section Council of the North Carolina Bar Association, the Board of Directors of Meredith College's Paralegal School, the Board of Directors of the Carolina Ballet, and the Women's Executive Mentoring Coalition. She is a North Carolina State Bar certified specialist in Family Law, a certified mediator in family financial cases, and was appointed by Governor Mike Easley to serve on the North Carolina Ethics Commission, effective October 2006. She was reappointed to the Ethics Commission by Governor Perdue in January of 2010. She was recently recognized by Business North Carolina magazine as one of the "Legal Elite" family law attorneys in North Carolina.

Ms. Stubbs is married to Tex Barrow and has two young sons. She is a runner and a good tennis player.

attorneys.name: Paul A. Suhr
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration & Naturalization Law Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Paul A. Suhr (서송해) is the son of the famous Korean poet Sea Jong-un (서정주), who wrote under the pen name Midang (미당). Paul was born in Korea and immigrated to the United States in January of 1966. He has resided in the state of North Carolina ever since and is a naturalized citizen of the United States. He received his Bachelor of Arts in English from Campbell College in 1969, his Master of Arts in English from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro in 1972, his Master of Science in Library Science from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1975, and his Juris Doctor from North Carolina Central University School of Law in 1988. He has practiced in the fields of immigration and family law for over 30 years.

Desde entonces ha residido en el estado de Carolina del Norte y es un ciudadano naturalizado de los Estados Unidos. Recibió su Bachillerato en Artes en inglés del Campbell College en 1969, su Maestría en Inglés en la Universidad de Carolina del Norte en Greensboro en 1972, su Maestría en Ciencias en Bibliotecología de la Universidad de Carolina del Norte en Chapel Hill en 1975, y su Doctor en Jurisprudencia de la Facultad de Derecho de la Universidad Central de Carolina del Norte en 1988. Ha ejercido en los campos de inmigración y derecho de familia durante más de 30 años.

attorneys.name: Dustin R.T. Sullivan
attorneys.practice_type: Driving While Impaired (DWI/DUI) Lawyers in Bolivia, NC
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Sullivan has handled tens of thousands of cases involving criminal defense, taking on a hands-on approach to his clients, dedicating himself to having his clients understand the process of their case. Mr. Sullivan has earned a number of awards on a national, state, and local level for his work in DWI Defense and Criminal Defense.

Mr. Sullivan handles a wide variety of cases, ranging from speeding tickets to class B1 felonies. Over the course of his career he has been televised on national television outlets for his criminal defense and has been televised on MTV's "Teen Mom 2". Mr. Sullivan has a great deal of trial experience which he brings to the table for each and every client Focusing his attention to only criminal defense and DWI cases, he fights to make sure his clients' rights are protected.

In 2001, Mr. Sullivan was accepted into the United States Army Reserve JAG Corps. However, after careful consideration and belief in "family first", he thought it appropriate to continue practicing law in the area he calls home.

Prior to becoming an attorney, Mr. Sullivan attended the University of Dayton in Dayton, Ohio, receiving multiple scholarships in football, academics, community service, and leadership. He played football all four years, where his team finished 18th in the nation for Division 1-AA. Mr. Sullivan attended the Appalachian School of Law in Grundy, Virginia where he was awarded for his services in Moot Court and Community Service as well as his membership in multiple organizations.

Dustin Sullivan worked at the Prosecutors Office in Cincinnati, OH for nearly four years and began his career in North Carolina working for the Brunswick County District Attorney's Office and New Hanover District Attorney's Office during and following law school. Mr. Sullivan also was a partner for over three years at Sullivan & Williams focusing on criminal defense.

Dustin RT Sullivan is an active member and strong supporter of the North Carolina Advocates for Justice.

attorneys.name: Matthew S. Sullivan
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Kinston, NC
attorneys.bio:
Matthew was born in Harrisonburg, Va. His primary area of practice is civil litigation and personal injury. Matt earned his undergraduate degree (B.S., magna cum laude) in administration of justice and public affairs in 1990, at Virginia Commonwealth University in Richmond, Va. He attended Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law at Campbell University where he was the Wiggins Scholar, Editor-in-Chief of the Campbell Law Review, Paul Dennis Award Recipient, and inducted into the International Order of Barristers. Matt received his Juris Doctor (magna cum laude) in 1995.

Matt has been selected to The Best Lawyers in America in the specialty of Product Liability Litigation since 2010. Matt was also recently selected by his peers for North Carolina Business Magazine Legal Elite for Litigation for 2013. About three percent of the State's attorneys are chosen as best practitioners, according to magazine officials.

Matt is licensed to practice before all North Carolina State Courts, the Federal District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit. He is a member of the North Carolina and American Bar Associations, the Eighth Judicial District Bar Association, the Lenoir County Bar Association (president 1997-1998), the North Carolina Advocates for Justice (member of Board of Governors), and The Eastern North Carolina Inn of Court.

Matt's practice is concentrated in the areas of catastrophic personal injury, industrial accidents, wrongful death, workers' compensation, commercial and general civil litigation.

Matt, married with three children, and his family attend Bethel Free Will Baptist Church. He is a member of the board of directors of the Lenoir Committee of 100 and has been involved in the United Way, Kinston Evening Rotary and the Kinston-Lenoir Chamber of Commerce. Matt has served on the North Carolina Advocates of Justice, Board of Governors, since 2008.

Matt continues his longtime love of athletics as head coach of the Carolina Tigers travel baseball team; earning a 1st degree black belt in jujitsu; hunting, fishing and shooting sports. He played collegiate baseball at Virginia Commonwealth University from 1986 through 1988.

In Recent Cases Note:

• Industrial Plant Explosion: Participated as co-lead counsel in obtaining $43,000,000 in compensation for the families and workers that were injured or killed in an industrial plant explosion that occurred at the West Pharmaceutical Services Kinston Plant on January 29, 2003.

• Acted as lead counsel in the Williams vs. Nationwide Mutual Ins. Co. matter that is the seminal case in North Carolina dealing with the insurance company's failure to provide an insured the opportunity to select or to reject underinsured motorist coverage. The North Carolina Appellate Courts affirmed the trial court's ruling extending insurance coverage to 1 Million dollars, the maximum allowed under North Carolina law. The Williams case resulting in sweeping changes to motorist's rights in North Carolina regarding uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage.

• Wrongful Death: Obtained a 13.3 million dollar judgment for the family of a man wrongfully killed in a nightclub shooting.

• Golf Course Accident: Resolved a crossing accident at a public golf course for a passenger in a golf cart for a large confidential six figure settlement.

• Tractor-Trailer Accident and Death: Obtained a large confidential settlement for the wrongful death of a retired military service member who was killed in an intersection accident, despite allegations of contributory negligence on behalf of the client, through detailed accident investigation and accident reconstruction.

• Bad Faith Refusal to Settle: Successfully protected a client insured’s personal assets, provided for the cancellation of an excess verdict and obtained a confidential personal settlement on behalf of the client against an insurance carrier, when the insurance carrier refused to resolve an underlying liability action against the client within the insurance policy limits.

• Construction Cases: Successfully represented a Fortune 500 company in obtaining substantial payment for work performed at a large scale coastal development that involved the developer, homeowners’ association, and 95 individual owners of property.

• Faulty Construction: Obtained a 2.2 Million dollar judgment related to the faulty construction of a sports fishing yacht.

He attended Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law at Campbell University where he was the Wiggins Scholar, Editor-in-Chief of the Campbell Law Review, Paul Dennis Award Recipient, and inducted into the International Order of Barristers. Matt received his Juris Doctor (magna cum laude) in 1995.

Matt has been selected to The Best Lawyers in America in the specialty of Product Liability Litigation since 2010. Matt was also recently selected by his peers for North Carolina Business Magazine Legal Elite for Litigation for 2013. About three percent of the State's attorneys are chosen as best practitioners, according to magazine officials.

Matt is licensed to practice before all North Carolina State Courts, the Federal District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit. He is a member of the North Carolina and American Bar Associations, the Eighth Judicial District Bar Association, the Lenoir County Bar Association (president 1997-1998), the North Carolina Advocates for Justice (member of Board of Governors), and The Eastern North Carolina Inn of Court.

Matt's practice is concentrated in the areas of catastrophic personal injury, industrial accidents, wrongful death, workers' compensation, commercial and general civil litigation.

Matt, married with three children, and his family attend Bethel Free Will Baptist Church. He is a member of the board of directors of the Lenoir Committee of 100 and has been involved in the United Way, Kinston Evening Rotary and the Kinston-Lenoir Chamber of Commerce. Matt has served on the North Carolina Advocates of Justice, Board of Governors, since 2008.

Matt continues his longtime love of athletics as head coach of the Carolina Tigers travel baseball team; earning a 1st degree black belt in jujitsu; hunting, fishing and shooting sports. He played collegiate baseball at Virginia Commonwealth University from 1986 through 1988.

In Recent Cases Note:

• Industrial Plant Explosion: Participated as co-lead counsel in obtaining $43,000,000 in compensation for the families and workers that were injured or killed in an industrial plant explosion that occurred at the West Pharmaceutical Services Kinston Plant on January 29, 2003.

• Acted as lead counsel in the Williams vs. Nationwide Mutual Ins. Co. matter that is the seminal case in North Carolina dealing with the insurance company's failure to provide an insured the opportunity to select or to reject underinsured motorist coverage. The North Carolina Appellate Courts affirmed the trial court's ruling extending insurance coverage to 1 Million dollars, the maximum allowed under North Carolina law. The Williams case resulting in sweeping changes to motorist's rights in North Carolina regarding uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage.

• Wrongful Death: Obtained a 13.3 million dollar judgment for the family of a man wrongfully killed in a nightclub shooting.

• Golf Course Accident: Resolved a crossing accident at a public golf course for a passenger in a golf cart for a large confidential six figure settlement.

• Tractor-Trailer Accident and Death: Obtained a large confidential settlement for the wrongful death of a retired military service member who was killed in an intersection accident, despite allegations of contributory negligence on behalf of the client, through detailed accident investigation and accident reconstruction.

• Bad Faith Refusal to Settle: Successfully protected a client insured’s personal assets, provided for the cancellation of an excess verdict and obtained a confidential personal settlement on behalf of the client against an insurance carrier, when the insurance carrier refused to resolve an underlying liability action against the client within the insurance policy limits.

• Construction Cases: Successfully represented a Fortune 500 company in obtaining substantial payment for work performed at a large scale coastal development that involved the developer, homeowners’ association, and 95 individual owners of property.

• Faulty Construction: Obtained a 2.2 Million dollar judgment related to the faulty construction of a sports fishing yacht.

attorneys.name: Jarrod Summey
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Jarrod was born and raised in the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina. He believes that community taught him a strong work ethic, the resilience of the North Carolina people, and the importance of not only caring for the community but being a trusted resource. Today, those strong values exhibit themselves in Jarrod’s willingness to take on complex cases for those harmed without shying away from the likelihood of trial. Jarrod prides himself on meeting his clients where they are by taking the time to explain the complexity of litigation.

During law school, Jarrod earned the Graduate Student Service Impact Award and the 3L Pro Bono Student of the Year Award for his strong commitment to public service and volunteer legal work in the community. He was also a founding student attorney of the Consumer Financial Transaction Clinic.

Prior to joining Maginnis Howard, Jarrod worked as an insurance defense litigator for a regional firm. The experience provided valuable insight on how cases are assessed for value and trial by opposing counsel and the insurance companies they represent. Jarrod began his career as an Assistant District Attorney at the Cabarrus County District Attorney’s Office. During his tenure, he successfully tried numerous felony cases and oversaw hundreds of bench trials. In addition to handling large felony caseloads, Jarrod became a critical asset due to his extensive knowledge of motor vehicle offenses.

Outside of work, Jarrod enjoys spending time with his wife and two daughters, fly fishing, being outdoors and exploring small beach towns.

attorneys.name: Robert W. Sumner
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Defense Litigation Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Bob Sumner has been practicing defense litigation in Raleigh, North Carolina since 1970. He has tried over 100 jury trials to conclusion with a very high number of successful outcomes. He has handled numerous wrongful death cases and cases involving catastrophic brain and spinal cord injuries. His cases have involved a wide range of activities: tractor/trailer accidents; workplace accidents; premises liability issues; fires and explosions; and product liability claims.

Bob holds the rank of “Advocate” in the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA), which is only given to lawyers who have tried at least 50 jury trials to conclusion as lead counsel. Rob also maintains an AV rating with Martindale Hubbell, the most prestigious peer review rating that recognizes attorneys who have reached the highest levels of skill and integrity.

Bob is currently listed in the publication, “The Best Lawyers in America ®,” 2006 and 2008 editions in the area of Personal Injury Litigation and 2009 edition in the areas of Personal Injury Litigation and Product Liability Litigation.

attorneys.bio:
Vernon Sumwalt has handled approximately 300 workers' compensation hearings, 120 appeals--mostly from cases he has tried--and many other cases before juries and our courts of general jurisdiction in both North Carolina and South Carolina. He is a Past President of the North Carolina Advocates for Justice (formerly the North Carolina Academy of Trial Lawyers) and has taught 145 state and national classes for lawyers and other professionals. He has also written over 55 books, chapters, and articles on different aspects of workers' compensation and trial law.

Since 2005, Vernon has been a North Carolina State Bar Board Certified Specialist in the area of Workers' Compensation Law. In 2014, the North Carolina State Bar also certified him as a Specialist in Appellate Practice.

attorneys.name: Barbara Szombatfalvy
attorneys.firm_name: Szombatfalvy Law, PLLC - Durham Family Law Firm
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Durham, NC
attorneys.bio:
Barbara Szombatfalvy graduated with honors from North Carolina Central School of Law in 2005. Since then, she has practiced family law as an associate with a Chapel Hill law firm, and from 2012 to 2025 as a partner of Woodmansee & Szombatfalvy, PLLC. As of July 2025, Barbara continues to provide family law services as part of Szombatfalvy Law, PLLC - Durham Family Law Firm.

Barbara works to establish strong, positive relationships with her clients and helps them navigate the emotional upheavals of divorce, achieve financial stability, and reduce the stress that divorce places on children. Whether in negotiation or litigation, she is a tough and determined advocate working to protect the best interests of her clients. In 2013, she gained certification as a Guardian Ad Litem and Parenting Coordinator.

Barbara is a member of the North Carolina State Bar, the North Carolina Bar Association, the Durham County Bar Association, the Orange County Bar Association, and the 16th Judicial District Bar and is recognized by Best Lawyers in America.

Barbara enjoys photography, hiking, and reading, and has been active rescuing and fostering stray and neglected dogs in the Triangle area. She takes great pleasure in exploring all of the great activities that Durham has to offer.

attorneys.name: Erica Miller Tallent
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Lincolnton, NC
attorneys.bio:
As a Lincoln County native, and West Lincoln High School graduate, Erica recognizes the importance of community. Divorces and separations can be one of the most stressful times of your life, and Erica finds it rewarding to be able to help her neighbors and community through these tumultuous times.

As one of the three lawyers in the family law team, Erica works to make sure clients understand the process, are educated on their options, and are represented to the best of their abilities. She recognizes that this is often a process no one wants to be involved in and works diligently to make sure everything is as seamless and efficient as possible. Johnathan Rhyne and Rebecca Yoder, the other two members of the family law team, are both certified by the North Carolina State Bar as specialist in family law, and all work together to employ strategies that will most effectively achieve your goals. In addition to the three attorneys, our paralegal staff, Bobbie and Brandi, have over 30 - and 20- years' experience with our firm, respectively.

Erica is a lifelong resident of Lincoln County, North Carolina and has been involved in the community since a young age. Since 2015, Erica has served her community as the director of the local Miss Lincoln County Apple Queen Pageant, awarding over $50,000 in scholarships to Lincoln County women. She is heavily involved in the Lincoln County Business Professional Women group, as well as other non-profit organizations in Lincoln County.

She graduated from Davidson College in 2019 with her B.A. She received her law degree (J.D. 2022) from The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, where she graduated in the Top 10 students, summa cum laude and was a member of the North Carolina Law Review. While in law school, Erica received the certificate of merit in her Personal Income Taxation course and was an enrichment group leader for both Contract and Real Property courses as well as an Honors Writing Scholar. Upon graduation, Erica was inducted into the Order of the Coif and accumulated over 100 hours of pro bono service hours.

In her free time, Erica enjoys spending time with her husband John Dock Tallent, and their puppy, Penelope. They enjoy going back to Davidson and Chapel Hill for sporting events on campus, as well as attending as many events downtown as they can.

attorneys.name: Brian R. Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lillington, NC
attorneys.bio:
Brian’s practice is primarily in the field of civil litigation. He has experience in handling matters ranging from personal injury claims to complex business disputes. Brian was born and raised in Lillington, North Carolina. He graduated from Harnett Central High School where he was a well-respected student-athlete. Brian was named as the News and Observer Student-Athlete of the Year in 2009 and 2010. Brian went on to North Carolina State University where he graduated cum laude and participated in football and baseball. Brian also completed an undergraduate degree at Campbell University where he participated in baseball. Brian went to law school at the Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law at Campbell University. During his time in law school, Brian was a legal research and writing scholar and top student. Brian graduated 10th in his class of 136.

After graduating from law school, Brian went on to work at a civil litigation firm in Raleigh, North Carolina. Brian gained valuable experience in handling a variety of civil matters. Brian gained recognition from his peers for the work that he performed during his time in Raleigh. He was named as One to Watch® by Best Lawyers® for 2023 in the field of Personal Injury Litigation. Brian made the decision to move back to his hometown to work in the community where he was raised. He sees it as a great honor to provide advice and counsel to those in need.

Since joining Bain & McRae, LLP in 2022, Brian has handled an impressive range of civil litigation matters. Brian has prevailed for his clients in jury trials, handled administrative appeals before local school boards, handled EEOC charges for local businesses, completed stock and asset purchase agreements, and handled various zoning matters from the application stage to appeals in Superior Court. Brian was named One to Watch® by Best Lawyers® for 2024, and 2025 in the field of Personal Injury Litigation.

attorneys.bio:
Stuart L. Teeter completed his undergraduate studies at East Carolina University in Greenville, North Carolina before obtaining his Juris Doctorate from Wake Forest University School of Law. In 1989, Attorney Stuart L. Teeter was admitted to the North Carolina Bar.

Since 1989, Attorney Stuart L. Teeter has built a reputation as a litigator. He has handled complex equitable distribution cases and custody cases. He has been involved in complex domestic litigation involving clients that have high net worth divorces. He has handled every level of criminal offense from traffic tickets to the most serious felonies. Attorney Teeter also represents Juveniles charged with crimes and is respected as a voice for the youth in the community. Additionally, he has resolved personal injury cases in the excess of one million dollars.

The combination of many years of experience and attention to detail makes Attorney Stuart L. Teeter a professional advocate and foreboding opponent in any courtroom whether it be Personal Injury, Family Law, or Criminal Law.

attorneys.name: Henry E. Teich
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Asheville, NC
attorneys.bio:
Hank has been in practice in Asheville with his law partner, Janson Grimes, for almost 40 years during which time his practice focused on Personal Injury Law. His primary focus now is Workers' Compensation Law and since 2000 he has been a North Carolina Board Certified Specialist in Workers' Compensation Law.

Hank's interest is making sure that his clients get the best medical treatment available under the circumstances and protecting them from oppressive insurance company tactics. He frequently represents workers whose injuries prevent them from returning to their previous jobs and who are in danger of not being able to work at all in the future.

He is a Member of the Board of Governors and a benefactor of the North Carolina Advocates for Justice. Hank is also Membership Chair of the Executive Committee of the Workers Compensation Section of the NC Advocates for Justice.

In 2007, 2010, 2016, 2017 and 2018 Hank received the Order of Service from the North Carolina Advocates for Justice, previously called The North Carolina Academy of Trial Lawyers. The award is given to members for generous contributions of service in advancing the Academy's mission of protecting people's rights.

Hank was selected for inclusion in the list of North Carolina Super Lawyers® in 2010, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2019.

Hank was included in the 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019 edition of Best Lawyers in America® for Workers Compensation Law-Claimants.

Hank was an Assistant County Attorney for Buncombe County in 1980-81 and in 1987 he was appointed Public Guardian. He retired from that position in 2007 after 20 years of service to incompetent adults and mentally disabled Veterans in Buncombe County and across North Carolina.

He is a former board member of Caring For Children and former advisory board member of the Asheville Lyric Opera. Hank is also a board member of the Mimosa Fishing Club and Marina at Lake James. He is married and has two daughters.

attorneys.name: Robin H. Terry
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Robin Terry has been handling workers' compensation matters for employers and workers' compensation carriers since 1993 when she joined Cranfill Sumner & Hartzog LLP. From 1990 to 1993, Robin represented plaintiffs in workers' compensation and personal injury matters. She has extensive experience at all levels of workers' compensation litigation including mediations, hearings, Full Commission arguments and other appellate levels.

Robin has handled hundreds of cases involving traumatic injuries by accident, occupational diseases, chemical exposures, claims for psychological/psychiatric injuries/conditions as well as permanent total issues such as attendant care and adaptive care.

Although Robin represents numerous workers' compensation carriers in various claims, a large part of her practice is devoted to representing several large self-insured employers including a poultry processor, a large medical facility, a municipality, a group of fast-food franchisors as well as a group of housing authorities.

North Carolina attorney's lifelong interest in law

Her experiences at these two firms were excellent opportunities that fueled her desire to become an attorney.

Marlo was also privileged to see another branch of government in action while working with Congressman Mike McIntyre as an intern during the summer of 2000.

attorneys.name: Frank C. Thigpen
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Southern Pines, NC
attorneys.bio:
After 53 years of dedicated service, Mr. Frank Thigpen retired from the practice of law on January 1, 2026. Mr. Frank Thigpen was a partner with the Law Firm of Thigpen & Jenkins, LLP. Mr. Thigpen began practice in 1972 in Robbins, North Carolina, and later in 1993 merged to form the Firm of Thigpen & Jenkins, LLP. Mr. Thigpen and his staff have helped thousands of individuals throughout Moore, Montgomery and the surrounding counties in an array of legal issues. The firm expanded to include three offices located in Southern Pines, Biscoe, and Robbins, North Carolina. Since Mr. Thigpen’s retirement, the Robbins location has closed, but the law firm of Thigpen & Jenkins continues to provide services through their Biscoe and Southern Pines offices.

Mr. Thigpen was born in 1945 and raised in Pikeville, NC. He graduated in 1968 from High Point University with a degree in History and Political Science. Later, he graduated from UNC School of Law in 1972. Shortly after that, Mr. Thigpen opened an office in Robbins, North Carolina, where he had a general practice and represented clients in criminal, family law, personal injury, worker’s compensation, business law, and real estate transactions. Mr. Thigpen was a member of the North Carolina Bar Association as well as a member of the North Carolina Advocates for Justice.

Mr. Thigpen has been married to his wife, Lynne, since 1968 and they have three grown children and are the proud grandparents of 9 grandchildren. He is a member of Southern Pines United Methodist Church where he has served for the past several years as Chairman of the Board. In his spare time, Mr. Thigpen enjoys traveling and spending time with his wife, children, and grandchildren.

attorneys.bio:
Sarah Thomas is an integral attorney with our firm, having graduated from the prestigious University of North Carolina School of Law, and she concentrates her practice in family law and general litigation. Having grown up in Wilson, North Carolina in a family esteemed attorneys, she has the heart of a litigator and is a true competitor in both her professional and personal lives.

In her youth, Sarah played tennis at an astonishingly high level, and traveled across the country for junior USTA tournaments. After moving to Chapel Hill to attend the University of North Carolina, she joined Chi Omega Sorority and was on the club tennis team. An illness late in high school led her to become involved with Teen Cancer America, and she became a Youth Ambassador for TCA her junior year at UNC. During her undergraduate career, she wrote for the Daily Tar Heel and the Lumina News. She graduated cum laude in 2016 with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism, and then attended the University of North Carolina School of Law beginning in the fall of 2016. During her time in law school, she participated in various prestigious academic and social groups and won awards for her hard work.

attorneys.name: Chase Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Chase Thompson is a motivated advocate who understands how important your case is to you. He represents people who have been injured at work, in car accidents, and in other circumstances.

Chase graduated from Radford University in 2019. During his time there, he served as a mentor to under-privileged students from a nearby high school through the Appalachian Arts and Studies in the Schools program. This experience taught him that helping others was the most fulfilling use of his time and talents.

Chase received his law degree from the University of South Carolina in 2023 and was admitted to the South Carolina Bar that same year. He is in the process of working towards admission to the North Carolina Bar. After graduating law school, Chase completed a judicial law clerk under the Honorable William McKinnon that gave him valuable exposure to civil law and trial practice. He then served the public as a prosecutor before joining Stewart Law Offices to serve injured victims.

When he is not working for clients, Chase enjoys spending his free time watching movies, golfing, and hiking. Crowder Mountain is one of his favorite nearby spots. He also enjoys watching the Charlotte Knights take on other teams at Truist Field. When you need a lawyer who will give your case the time and effort it deserves, contact Chase Thompson and the legal professionals at Stewart Law Offices.

attorneys.name: Bryan Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Winston-Salem, NC
attorneys.bio:
After just one year as an associate with Surratt and Thompson, PLLC, Bryan Thompson became a member of the firm. He was appointed Public Administrator of Forsyth County, North Carolina in 2006 and Public Administrator of Davie County, North Carolina in 2010, providing estate administration and guardianship services as an independent person when required by the Court.

His legal practice areas are broad and include the following: Elder Law, Wills and Estate Planning, Trusts and Estates, Guardianship, Corporate Law, Collections, Taxation, Consumer Law, and Residential / Commercial Real Estate. Bryan chairs the firm's Estate, Guardianship, and Trust practices.

Bryan has had the privilege of representing clients in state and federal courts as well as numerous federal and state regulatory bodies. As a trusted attorney, Bryan has been appointed several times to wind down law firms of attorneys.

In addition to his legal practice, Bryan is actively involved in his community serving on the Advisory Board of the Salvation Army in Winston-Salem (past Chair), the Stewardship Committee of River Oaks Community Church, the Human Rights Committee of Centerpoint Human Services (current Chair), the Board of Directors of the North Carolina Guardianship Association (current President and Chair), and the Board of Directors for Trellis Foundation (Secretary).

Bryan was appointed to the Governing Board of Cardinal Innovations, the largest medicaid managed organization in the State of North Carolina, in September, 2016. He served on the 2013 DHHS, Division of Aging and Adult Services Ad Hoc Guardianship Workgroup and is an active speaker and presenter for various professional conferences on the topics of public health, governmental programs and elder / disability law.

Most importantly, Bryan is married to Sharon Thompson and is the father of two daughters, Nina and Sophia, with whom he meanders around the world experiencing new cultures, and making new friends.

Lawrence founded Tickle Law Office in 2013 after graduating from Campbell University School of Law and passing the North Carolina State Bar. Lawrence earned his Bachelor of Science in Political Science from East Carolina University in 2010 as well as his Master of Science in Criminal Justice and Public Administration from Liberty University in 2015. Lawrence served in the United States Marine Corps after high school where he learned the essential leadership and management skills necessary to be successful as a zealous advocate for his clients. A native of Reidsville, NC, Lawrence now calls Franklin County home. He prides himself in fighting for the little guy and helping others. A true problem solver, Lawrence repairs automobiles and other mechanical items in his free time.

Lawrence vigorously fights for you in the court room whether it is a misdemeanor, DWI, or felony or whether you are fighting for your children or you livelihood during divorce. If your legal matter is important to you, make an appointment to visit Tickle Law Office by calling the office, filling out the email form or chatting with an agent right now.

attorneys.name: Emma Tillotson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Durham, NC
attorneys.bio:
Emma Tillotson did not know she would find her calling in family law. Emma received her undergraduate degree from Clemson University cum laude in Psychology and Criminal Justice, with a minor in Sociology. She left her home state of South Carolina to attend the Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law at Campbell University, where she graduated cum laude. During her legal studies she found her passion representing people going through difficult family transitions. She participated in the family law clinic representing underprivileged residents of Raleigh in their family law needs, was an active member of Law Students Against Sexual Assault and Domestic Violence, serving as Vice President, was a student mentor and was an active member of the award-winning Mock Trial team.

“Sexual assault and domestic violence are prevalent in our community, and it is imperative that individuals understand they are not alone and that there exists a path to safety and recovery. Collaborating with survivors is profoundly gratifying and has enhanced my understanding of how to better serve the community. I believe that the practice of family law transcends mere legal processes, and I am dedicated to supporting families during their most challenging times.” – Emma Tillotson

In her leisure time, Emma enjoys engaging with family and friends, caring for her cat, Wilkie, reading, and exploring the outdoors.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Rebecca Ann Phillips Memorial Award (2024)

attorneys.name: Daniel B. Titsworth
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cary, NC
attorneys.bio:
Daniel Titsworth is also a graduate of Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law at Campbell University and owner of Titsworth Law Offices, P.A. Dan has been representing injured people since 1994 in all aspects of injury law, including those in traffic accidents and on-the-job injuries. His involvement in these claims begins at the initial client meeting and, if necessary, proceeds all the way through to jury trial. He is also a member of the North Carolina State Bar, North Carolina Advocates for Justice, 10th Judicial Bar Association and the Wake County Bar Association.

Dan enjoys becoming familiar with each client and is a very hands-on attorney. He grew up in a working family in a small Illinois town, which provided the basis for developing the concept of having a law firm with “Lawyers You Can Talk To.” He prefers his clients call him by his first name and he talks to them in a language they understand. Dan believes effective representation begins by taking the time to get to know the client. Many of his clients have kept in touch with him through the years and have referred their family and friends.

attorneys.name: D. Kenneth Tisdale Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: DWI Lawyers in Winston-Salem, NC
attorneys.bio:
D. Kenneth (Ken) Tisdale, Jr., joined Grace, Tisdale & Clifton in 2002 and has dedicated much of his practice to Driving While Impaired (DWI) defense and alcohol-related charges. From 1997 to 2002, Ken served as an Assistant District Attorney in Winston-Salem and focused on the prosecution of DWI cases, as well as felony trials in Superior Court, including capital murder. He has extensive expertise in the area of DWI law both as a defense attorney and prosecutor, including a large volume of trials at the District Court and Superior Court level.

Ken has been trained in the administration of DWI field tests, including the horizontal gaze nystagmus test. Every day he assists numerous individuals with his skills in the art of determining the best course of action for North Carolina DWI issues in order to dispense with cases in the most efficient and discreet manner possible.

In addition to his DWI representation, Ken has substantial trial experience in N.C. District and Superior Courts for a range of criminal cases including murder, drugs, sexual assault and financial crimes.

Ken received his Juris Doctorate from Wake Forest University School of Law in 1997 and his Bachelor of Arts degree in Business Management from North Carolina State University in 1993. He has been admitted to practice in North Carolina since 1997 and has been admitted to practice in the U.S. District Court, Middle District.

Ken is a member of the North Carolina Academy of Trial Lawyers, the North Carolina Bar Association, the North Carolina State Bar and the Forsyth County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Carrie Tortora
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Carrie Tortora grew up in Louisiana and earned a degree in accounting from Louisiana State University. After attending the UNC School of Law, she settled in Raleigh.

Carrie is a board-certified family law specialist with nearly fifteen years of experience as a divorce and family law attorney. After working in a boutique family law firm for many years, Carrie made the decision to launch Tortora Family Law because she is passionate about supporting people through some of the most stressful and difficult events in their lives.

Carrie’s background in accounting provides her a unique skill set to handle the financial issues involved in divorce, including valuing and dividing business interests and calculating support. She also clerked at the North Carolina Court of Appeals following law school, which experience provided her insight into the inner workings of the court system.

When Carrie is not practicing law, she enjoys spending time with her husband, Frank, and juggling the joy and chaos that comes with having three young children and one old beagle. She also enjoys traveling and learning about new places and cultures, and watching standup comedy.

attorneys.name: Benton L. Toups
attorneys.practice_type: Alternative Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Wilmington, NC
attorneys.bio:
Benton is a partner in the firm’s Wilmington office. His practice concentrates on representing businesses in all aspects of labor and employment law. He has represented employers before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Department of Labor, the North Carolina Industrial Commission, and several state and federal courts.

He has extensive experience assisting employers with claims of discrimination and harassment under Title VII, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and the North Carolina Retaliatory Employment Discrimination Act (REDA), as well as claims for unpaid wages and overtime pursuant to the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

In addition to defending existing claims, Benton routinely counsels employers on day-to-day issues and assists them in developing and implementing effective policies in order to avoid employment litigation. He has spoken to businesses, attorneys, and insurers on claims avoidance and litigation strategy.

Benton was selected by Business North Carolina magazine as a North Carolina Legal Elite in the field of Employment Law in 2010 and 2011. He was also named one of North Carolina’s 2009, 2010 and 2011 Rising Stars in Employment and Labor Law.

Fuchsberg Law Center, where she was recognized for her commitment to public service.

Devin was honored with the Clinician of the Year award for her exceptional dedication to supporting clients. She also served as the Research Editor for her law school’s journal.

During her legal studies, Devin gained valuable experience in litigation, client advocacy, and legal writing, working with federal defenders, public interest organizations, and law clinics.

Devin takes a client-centered approach to her practice, ensuring that each client receives tailored attention and strong advocacy. Licensed to practice in North Carolina, she brings determination, and a problem-solving mindset to every case, working tirelessly to achieve the best possible outcomes.

Outside the office, Devin is actively involved in statewide educational justice efforts, advocating for equitable access to education. When she’s not working, she enjoys practicing yoga, and soaking up the Wilmington sunshine.

attorneys.name: Damian L. Tucker
attorneys.firm_name: Hester & Tucker, PLLC Attorneys at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Traffic Tickets Lawyers in Rocky Mount, NC
attorneys.bio:
Damian L. Tucker was sworn in as an Assistant District Attorney for Nash, Edgecombe and Wilson Counties (Seventh Judicial District) in September 1998. He prosecuted cases from routine traffic matters to violent felony cases, including homicide cases. After three years as a prosecutor, he joined the law firm of Hester & Tucker, PLLC in 2001. In 2007, he became a partner in the firm which is now Hester & Tucker, PLLC.

Damian's sole concentration is defending the criminally accused in the Seventh Judicial District. He also has handled some matters in civil, child support and small claims courts. During this period of his practice, he has resolved thousands of traffic matters and misdemeanors at the District Court level. Also, Damian has successfully defended clients charged with serious felony charges at the trial level. He has extensive jury trial experience to include cases involving traffic and misdemeanor offenses, as well as the most serious drug and "violent" felony offenses, including homicide cases. He is also a board certified specialist in state criminal law.

Damian L. Tucker has been a lifelong resident of Nash County. He currently lives in the Dortches, NC community with his wife, Chandra, who is a veterinarian, and sons, Nicholas and Jacob.

He has always been involved in his community in an effort to make it a better place to live. He makes it a priority to speak at the local schools to educate youth on how choices can affect their future goals.

He also has spoken at Saint Augustine's College (Raleigh, NC), North Carolina Central University School of Law (Durham, NC), and participated with the TEEN COURT program in this district.

Damian is a life member of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. and has served as general counsel for the Middle Eastern Province of Kappa Alpha Psi since 2011.

attorneys.name: Shannon Ashburn Tucker
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Durham, NC
attorneys.bio:
Shannon Tucker has been practicing law in North Carolina since 1993. After graduating from UNC, where she majored in ancient and medieval history and minored in English literature, she attended UNC School of Law. She handled a combination of family law and criminal law cases prior to serving in the Office of the Public Defender in Durham County. She has an extensive amount of courtroom experience, appearing in both District and Superior Courts on a regular basis. Although she has obtained great verdicts for her clients at trial and has successfully argued cases in the NC Court of Appeals, and the North Carolina Supreme Court, she believes that her greatest skill is her empathy, and her ability to have compassion for and to bond with her clients in their time of need.

Shannon believes strongly in giving back to her community and has served in the Junior League of Durham and Orange Counties since 2002, serving as league President from 2011-2012. She has served on the Board of Communities In Schools of Durham, as Main Event Co-Chair of Band Together, and has volunteered with Caring House Gala and the Animal Protection Society of Durham for many years. In her free time Shannon loves reading, gardening, traveling, playing tennis with her husband and cheering for their daughter at her polo matches.

attorneys.name: Jason Tuttle
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury and Wrongful Death Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Jason Tuttle is a North Carolina attorney with more than two decades of experience representing individuals in both personal injury and business litigation matters. He finds personal injury to be particularly rewarding because it allows him the opportunity to assist accident victims through the difficult times that arise when an injury has disrupted their lives.

As both an attorney and a counselor at law, Jason believes it is an attorney's role to advise clients not just on their legal matters, but also, to acknowledge the collateral consequences of a case on a person's life. He works closely with Ed Gaskins and other members of Gaskins Hancock Tuttle Hash LLP to ensure we not only advise our clients legally, but also, marshal them through the personal challenges their cases present.

Jason is an active member of the Wake County Bar Association, where he chairs the Athletics Committee and previously served on the Board of Directors. He has been a Guest Lecturer at both North Carolina State University and the UNC School of Law, and is honored to be AV-rated by Martindale-Hubbell for his legal ability and commitment to ethical standards in his practice.

Jason currently lives in Raleigh with his wife and three sons.

Past Results Include:

$1,600,000 settlement for motorcyclist injured in collision caused by a distracted driver resulting in below the knee amputation of the left leg (2022)

$425,000 settlement for young woman who fell on defective exit ramp outside of a popular NC bar, suffering a fractured foot that led to Complex Regional Pain Syndrome ("CRPS") (2022)

$251,500 settlement of worker's compensation claim for woman injured after slip and fall at work resulting in low back surgery and CRPS (2022)

$710,000 global settlement for a high school student, who suffered permanent partial vision loss as a result of an incident in gym class (2021)

$250,000 settlement for a minor child and and mother, after her child was injured in a drive-by shooting of a home daycare where the child was a participant (2019)

$1,066,666 policy limits settlement for estates of husband and wife killed in a rollover automobile accident (2016)

$240,000 in settlements of personal injury and worker's compensation claims for slip and fall at work resulting in left shoulder rotator cuff tear surgery with CRPS (2016)

$350,000 arbitration award for teenager injured by a distracted driver resulting in a traumatic brain injury and post-traumatic headache syndrome (2015)

$155,000 settlement for a woman injured by a City of Raleigh garbage truck resulting in a left ulnar fracture requiring surgery (2012)

DISCLAIMER: The outcome of a particular case cannot be predicated upon a lawyer's or a law firm's past results. Past results should not be construed as a representation that we will be successful with any particular case in the future, and not every case in which we have been involved has resulted in a favorable outcome. Settlements are the result of private negotiations between the parties involved that may be affected by factors other than the legal merits of a particular case.

attorneys.name: Meghan A. Van Vynckt
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Meghan understands that clients come to her for guidance through extremely difficult and emotional times, and that it requires superb legal advice, professionalism, and client service to obtain desirable results for each client. While Meghan believes it is best to resolve most matters outside of the courtroom, Meghan is prepared to advocate for her clients in the courtroom if needed.

Representing clients primarily with family law matters, Meghan has experience in various areas of family law including separation, divorce, child custody and support, alimony, equitable distribution, pre-nuptial agreements, post-nuptial agreements, and other family law matters.

Meghan is a native Charlottean who grew up on Lake Norman. She graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill with a Bachelor's in Journalism and Political Science. After graduation, Meghan returned to Charlotte and graduated with honors from Charlotte School of Law. Meghan now resides in Charlotte and is passionate about serving clients in Mecklenburg and surrounding counties.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Raleigh, North Carolina Traffic Defense Attorney

Timothy Vanderweert is a Raleigh, North Carolina lawyer practicing in DWI and traffic defense. He has been representing clients for twenty-one (21) years, throughout Wake County and the Triangle area, including Wake, Durham, Orange and Johnston County courts.

Mr. Vanderweert is a 1990 graduate of the University of North Carolina School of Law at Chapel Hill, where he attended on a Van Hecke Scholarship. He has also earned degrees in the Humanities from Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, and from the Graduate School of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

Since beginning his practice of the law in 1990, he has been practicing almost exclusively in DWI and traffic defense. Over the course of his legal career, Mr. Vanderweert has represented over 20,000 people in traffic court.

attorneys.name: John Carl Vermitsky
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Winston-Salem, NC
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Vermitsky received his undergraduate degree from the University of Rochester located in Rochester, NY where he graduated with honors with a dual degree in Spanish Language and Culture and Political Science. While he was enrolled at the University of Rochester Mr. Vermitsky received the distinction of Academic All American for his national success in intercollegiate debate.

After college, Mr. Vermitsky attended Wake Forest University School of Law where he graduated cum laude. While enrolled at Wake, Mr. Vermitsky was an active member of the local trial bar and served as a staff member of the Wake Forest University Law Review. Upon graduation, Mr. Vermitsky was named a member of Wake Forest University's chapter of the Order of the Coif, an honor fraternity reserved for those who graduate in the top 10% of the law school's graduating class. Mr. Vermitsky passed the North Carolina Bar in July of 2006, and began practicing with Morro Porter Vermitsky & Taylor, PLLC shortly thereafter.

Mr. Vermitsky's practice focuses on civil trial law of all types. He regularly practices in both Federal and State trial courts, appellate court, and handles the following types of claims: wrongful death, insurance coverage, breach of contract, civil rights, motorsport and sports litigation, malpractice, breach of fiduciary duties and shareholder claims, and many other types of complex civil litigation.

Mr. Vermitsky is also a North Carolina board certified specialist in Family Law and handles all elements of domestic litigation from custody to alimony, to property division and everything in between. Additionally, Mr. Vermitsky has had considerable experience representing spouses who are involved with claims of alienation of affections and criminal conversation and has persuaded at least one trial court to find that these torts are unconstitutional.

As a proud Demon Deacon, Mr. Vermitsky teaches trial practice at Wake Forest School of Law and is clinic supervisor in the litigation clinic.

Originally from Budd Lake, New Jersey Mr. Vermitsky and his family have called North Carolina their home for over a decade. His hobbies include teaching Karate, spending time with his wife and children, traveling and cheering on his favorite sports teams, the New York Jets and Demon Deacons.

attorneys.name: Robin F. Verhoeven Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Chapel Hill, NC
attorneys.bio:
Robin Verhoeven, who has more than 25 years of experience, received her Juris Doctorate degree from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Law in 1998. While in law school, Robin Verhoeven honed her writing and oral argument skills by competing successfully with the Philip C. Jessup International Law Moot Court team and the Manfred Lachs Space Law Moot Court teams. Individually and as part of a team, Robin won accolades for writing and oral arguments at both the national and international level. Also, while in law school, Robin Verhoeven worked with the North Carolina Coalition Against Sexual Assault (NCCASA); first as the Legislative Intern and later as their Interim Executive Director. She is exceptionally proud of her contributions with NCCASA involving the inception of the Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) PROGRAM IN North Carolina. Robin Verhoeven owned her own family law firm prior to joining Donna Ambler Davis, P.C. and also worked with the Franklin Law Center prior to Susan R. Franklin's retirement. Robin Verhoeven is licensed to practice in all District and Superior Courts in North Carolina and is also licensed to practice in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina.

"People often ask how I can practice family law, because they assume (correctly!) that it is an emotionally difficult area of law for an attorney. My response is that I have an above-average sense of humor and an easily accessible and well-appointed happy place. Both are true. I believe that laughter is the best medicine and I can conjure up an image of sitting on a peaceful beach somewhere in a skinny minute - this is a good trick when you're having your blood pressure monitored at the doctor's office, by the way. Family law clients are often in the midst of the most difficult time periods in their lives. I tell them that I cannot promise that the process (whether that process is negotiation, mediation, or litigation) will be easy or fun. But I can promise two things; that we will get through it together and that they will experience a great relief whenever the outstanding issues are resolved. In the journey of each family law matter, the client is the captain of his or her own ship. I see my role as a family law attorney as being up in the crow's nest of each client's own personal ship, with my eyes focused on the horizon (i.e. the resolution of the case) and providing guidance through the tumultuous seas of uncertainty to the peaceful shore of resolution."

attorneys.name: Branch W. Vincent III
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Southern Shores, NC
attorneys.bio:
I have been practicing law since 1986. The first case I handled was a worker's compensation case. I have spent the last 38 years representing injured and disabled clients in cases involving worker's compensation, personal injury, social security disability, wrongful death, sexual harassment, race and age discrimination, excessive force by law enforcement and lawsuits involving insurance companies.

I am one of 68 lawyers in North Carolina who has been certified by the North Carolina State Bar as a Specialist in Workers Compensation Law, and have had this designation since 2000.

I formed a new law firm in January 2005 to continue practicing law in these areas. We will use our experience with medical issues and the medical community and our history of negotiations and trials with the insurance industry to benefit you in your injury case.

In addition to appearing in the trial courts of North Carolina, I have also appeared in numerous cases before United States District Court, the North Carolina Industrial Commission, the North Carolina Court of Appeals, the North Carolina Supreme Court and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit.

attorneys.name: Brian Walsh
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Brian Walsh was raised in North Canton, Ohio. However, his roots began in Annapolis, Maryland, which he will always consider his “home.” Growing up Brian played nearly every sport under the sun, but found his true passion in track and cross country, including being a collegiate athlete. Though he has since hung up his running spikes he still enjoys running and participates in marathons.

Brian graduated from Miami University with a Bachelor’s in Political Science and a minor in History. While at Miami Brian volunteered with St. Mary’s Catholic Church and other Catholic charities in southwest Ohio. Brian graduated from Campbell University School of Law in 2024. While at Campbell Brian served as chair of the Student Bar Association’s Diversity Committee as well as the Student Life Committee. Brian also provided Pro-bono legal services in the Gailor Law Family Litigation Clinic and the Blanchard Community Criminal Law Clinic. Brian has dedicated his life to the service of others, always offering a helping hand when someone is in need.

Brian believes family law is a calling–one in which he aims to provide not only superior legal services, but also provide the compassion required during major life events. Brian handles all areas of family law, including divorce, separation, child support, child custody, domestic violence, equitable distribution, post separation support/alimony, and prenuptial agreements.

Aside from practicing law, Brian enjoys snowboarding, watching sports (go canes), spending time with his family, and cooking.

attorneys.name: Louis A. Waple II
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
Lou is a life-long North Carolina resident, raised in Fayetteville. He graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and received his law degree from Campbell University. From the initial steps of his professional career, he has worked in the courtroom. He served as an assistant district attorney in Mecklenburg County. From there, Lou joined a small but growing civil litigation defense firm in 2001, where he started his workers' compensation practice, representing employers and insurance companies throughout the state. He was a partner in what became a large multi-state civil litigation firm. In 2008, Lou joined a growing statewide personal injury firm, where he opened and managed the Charlotte office, and helped injured employees pursue their workers' compensation claims against their employers and the insurance carriers. The time working and serving clients in large, volume practices, on both sides of workers' compensation issues, provided invaluable experience that Lou now shares within a smaller practice setting, one with less volume but more client accessibility. In addition to the central focus on workers' compensation, Lou expanded his practice in 2013 to become a mediator, to help parties resolve their Workers' Compensation Litigation.

Just like many members of our community, Lou is active in community organizations to include his church, the Mecklenburg County Bar and coaching youth sports. He has enjoyed his time serving on Mecklenburg County Bar's Grievance and Fee Dispute Committees.

attorneys.name: S. Denise Watts
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning/Estate Administration Lawyers in Shallotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
S. Denise Watts is an attorney who focuses her practice on serving the estate planning, estate administration, probate, and homeowners/property owners' association issues for the citizens and residents of North Carolina and South Carolina. She earned her Juris Doctor degree from North Carolina Central University School of Law in 2002, where she was managing editor of the North Carolina Central University Law Review.

After successfully completing the North Carolina bar exam, Mrs. Watts joined a general practice firm in Wake County, North Carolina where she practiced law in five counties: Wake, Johnston, Nash, Franklin, and Wilson. This experience gave Mrs. Watts a wealth of trial experience. In 2006, Mrs. Watts was sworn in as a member of the United States Supreme Court Bar and moved to Brunswick County, North Carolina to practice law, where she continues today as the Managing Partner of Watts Law Group PLLC.

In 2013, after successfully completing the South Carolina bar exam, Mrs. Watts and the firm of Watts Law Group PLLC opened a law office in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina to provide legal services. At Watts Law Group PLLC, Mrs. Watts counsels individuals on their estate planning issues, which may include the drafting of the following documents: a durable power of attorney, a health care power of attorney, a health care directive, a living will, a revocable living trust agreement, an irrevocable trust agreement, a supplemental needs trust, a special needs trust, a QTIP trust, an AB trust also known as bypass trust and a Last Will and Testament. Mrs. Watts also provides representation to homeowners/property owners' associations regarding issues such as drafting declarations, formation and termination of associations, filing claim of liens, handling disputes with property owners, filing foreclosures for unpaid assessments; filing lawsuits regarding owners failure to comply with the governing laws of the state and the association, and interpreting the Master Declaration and/or restrictive covenants for an association in regards to the Association's rights and remedies.

Mrs. Watts is an active member of the following professional organizations: the United States Supreme Court Bar, the North Carolina State Bar, the South Carolina Bar, the 15th Judicial District Bar Association, and the Brunswick County Bar Association. She received her Bachelor of Science degree in Mathematics from Meredith College in 1999, magna cum laude, and has worked in a law firm since she was sixteen. Mrs. Watts treats every client with respect and integrity, and each client's case is treated with exceptional care and attention.

Mrs. Watts is a happy person, full of energy, and very aggressive. Mrs. Watts is very open, easy to talk to and is very attentive to her clients. During Mrs. Watts' spare time, she enjoys spending time with her family, attending church, riding bikes, and participating in any activity of at the beach-especially beach/pool volleyball.

attorneys.name: Woody White
attorneys.practice_type: Serious Automobile Accidents and Personal Injury Lawyers in Wilmington, NC
attorneys.bio:
Woody White is a senior partner with Woody White Law PLLC, a general practice, courtroom-based attorney. For more than 30 years, Woody has litigated serious criminal, personal injury, and business cases in both state and federal court. HIs practice is located in Wilmington, North Carolina, just before the bridge to Wrightsville Beach. He handles cases involving motor vehicle accidents, damages against drunk drivers, bicycle accidents, as well as those charged with criminal offenses in either state or federal court.

Woody also counsels top corporations in crisis management and business strategy.

Among his many accomplishments, Mr. White is a former North Carolina state senator, having been appointed by the governor of North Carolina to serve in the legislature in 2004. He has been recognized by Business North Carolina magazine as a member of its “LEGAL ELITE”, winning the award in 2007, 2010 and 2021.

Woody was elected and served two terms as a New Hanover County Commissioner from 2012 - 2020, receiving the most votes in a 6 way contested election. At his first meeting, he was unanimously selected by his fellow commissioners as Chairman of the New Hanover Board of Commissioners. Woody has also served as a Board of Trustees Member for the University of North Carolina at Wilmington (UNCW) as well as Cape Fear Community College (CFCC).

In March of 2023, supported by President Pro Temp Phil Berger of North Carolina Senate, Woody was appointed to a four year term on the University of North Carolina Board of Governors.

Woody was also appointed in 2023 by the New Hanover County Commission to be a Director of the New Hanover Community Endowment.

As a Board Certified Specialist in State and Federal Criminal Law, Mr. White has extensive courtroom experience and has won numerous jury trials. He has litigated countless suppression motions and bond hearings and has represented thousands of defendants charged with violent crimes, white collar offenses, drug offenses, and literally everything in between. He is an active member of the North Carolina Bar Association and the National Criminal Defense Attorneys Association, and he has served extensively on local boards in the Wilmington community.

Mr. White is a lifelong resident of Southeastern North Carolina and received his law degree from the University of Nebraska. He is licensed to practice before the state bar of North Carolina, the Eastern District of the U.S. District Court, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit and was sworn into the United States Supreme Court by the late Chief Justice William Rehnquist.

Please visit my other website http://www.wilmingtonpersonalinjurylaw.com/ for more information.

attorneys.name: Robert A. Whitlow
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
For over 30 years, Robert has been zealously representing people with serious health conditions that force them to stop working. He has won thousands of disability claims and knows what it takes to prove and collect social security disability and long term disability benefits (the success of each case is determined on its own merits). Robert will work with your doctors to develop the kind of evidence needed to win. He is not part of a huge, impersonal law firm. He gives each client personal attention, answers questions, and returns phone calls.

Robert has extensive experience in social security disability and long term disability claims. He has assisted thousands of individuals at all levels of the administrative process, from hearings through the federal appellate courts.

A published author, Robert has written novels in the legal/suspense genre, several of which have been adapted into film. Additional information about this aspect of his activities is available at robertwhitlow.com.

attorneys.name: Douglas Q. Wickham
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Douglas Q. Wickham is one of the most experienced bankruptcy attorneys in the Raleigh, North Carolina area. He has been certified as a specialist in both consumer and business bankruptcy by the North Carolina State Bar since 1987. He is admitted to practice in North Carolina, as well as before all North Carolina federal courts and the U.S Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit.

Doug earned a bachelor's degree in History from Yale University. He received his law degree from the Yale Law School and earned an LLM at the Harvard Law School. He was a professor at the University of Tennessee College of Law for over 15 years teaching a variety of classes including civil procedure, commercial law, debtor-creditor law and municipal law. While in academia, he published numerous articles in major law reviews and served in the University Senate.

Doug and his family moved to Raleigh in 1987 where he entered the private practice of law. He has been a member of the Sanford, Adams, McCullough & Beard; Hatch, Little, & Bunn; and Stubbs & Perdue law firms. Since 2018 he has maintained his own law office as a sole practitioner, continuing to personally assist clients who need bankruptcy help.

Doug is a member of the North Carolina Bar Association and its Bankruptcy Section, serving on several committees and in various leadership roles over the years. He is a member of the Wake County Bar Association which recognized him as a 50-year practicing lawyer in 2018. He is recognized as a 10-year Super Lawyer. He has been a member of the American Bar Association, previously serving on its business bankruptcy and commercial financial services committees.

Doug's experience and personal attention to his clients are the hallmarks of his practice.

attorneys.name: Jordan S. Wideman
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Charlotte, NC
attorneys.bio:
To me, family doesn’t have one definition. Family is always what you want it to be. Family for me, has never been about blood relation. My family was comprised of people that were worthy of my love and attention, because they reciprocated it. But no matter who they were, those that are family, mean the world to me. It always allowed me to empathize with others about how they should want to protect their own families.

Public Service is something that runs in blood. My father has over 30 years of service as both a firefighter and policeman. My mother was a social worker in child support and my brother is currently a firefighter. Though I never expressed it out loud, being a family law attorney seemed destined for me. Extending a helping hand is all I saw my entire life.

Prior to having my law degree, I worked with youth programs with kids. This was the first time I recognized my desire to care for others. In child education and services, I took on a role of being somewhat of an extended family member for a lot of those kids and their families. That desire to preserve and help a family, never left me.

My entire life I watched those close to me help others in their time of need. Being a help to others is a natural passion of mine, I couldn’t turn it off if I tried. Family law allows me the chance to not only help people, but to reassure them that they still have control over what is most important to them, family.

I am the first attorney in my family, but this accomplishment was the reward of more than just my hard work. My hard work at Modern Legal is a symbol of my families love and support allowing me to achieve my passion every day. That same love and support is an additional motivation to have me carry out my passion by advocating for the families that come into the office.

Mallory Willink was born and raised in Morgantown, West Virginia, and graduated from West Virginia University with a Bachelors of Science in Public Relations in 2009. While at West Virginia University, Mallory was a member of Alpha Omicron Pi sorority, and a member of the Debate Team. Mallory attended and graduated from The Charlotte School of Law, and was admitted to the North Carolina bar in 2012. While there, Mallory served as the 4th Circuit Governor for the American Bar Association Law Student Division, was the editor in chief for the Charlotte Law Docket, interned with the Honorable Russell M. Clawges, Jr. of the 17th Judicial Circuit in West Virginia and completed over 140 hours of pro bono service. Upon graduating law school, Mallory accepted a position with a family law firm in Union County where she focused on criminal and family law. While in Union County, Mallory served as a member of the Union County Community Shelter’s Boots & Bowties Committee to assist in the planning of that event. Mallory is currently helping to plan the 1st annual pumpkin carving contest for the 4th Annual Ballantyne Festival, located in the Ballantyne District Park in October.

Mallory enjoys being active in the community, and spending time with her husband and “Chiweenie,” Nina. She is also a passionate Buffalo Bills and West Virginia Mountaineers fan. In her spare time, Mallory enjoys traveling and playing golf with her husband.

attorneys.name: Huntington M. Willis
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Raleigh, NC
attorneys.bio:
Hunt grew up in the mountains of North Carolina. After receiving his undergraduate degree from Appalachian State University, Hunt was commissioned as an officer in the United States Army, where he served as a captain. He is a former intelligence officer and veteran of the Iraq War.

Hunt's practice focuses on representing real people who have been harmed by the negligence of others, including from tractor-trailer collisions, car wrecks, defective products and construction accidents. He has successfully tried numerous cases to verdict for his clients before juries across the state of North Carolina. In fact, Hunt’s trial team won jury verdicts of $3.35 million, $1.25 million, and $250,325 in 2014 alone. Hunt has also obtained numerous million dollar settlements for his clients.

His practice includes a wide variety of areas, from product liability and wrongful death to commercial trucking litigation and insurance coverage disputes. He is licensed to practice in all North Carolina courts, as well as all federal courts in North Carolina and the United States Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit. He is an active member of the North Carolina Bar Association, the North Carolina Advocates for Justice, the American Association for Justice, and the Southern Trial Lawyers Association.

Hunt graduated cum laude from Campbell University School of Law. While in law school, he was managing editor of the Campbell Law Review and a member of the national moot court team. Hunt served as an extern to the Honorable Rick Elmore of the North Carolina Court of Appeals, and upon graduation was inducted into the Order of Barristers. He was later awarded the Safran Moot Court Award by the law school for outstanding contribution to the school's appellate advocacy program. Hunt has been recognized by Super Lawyers every year since 2016 as a Rising Star.

Hunt lives in Raleigh with his wife and daughter. In their free time, they love traveling, fitness, and the outdoors.

attorneys.name: Catherine Loden Wilson
attorneys.firm_name: McPherson, Rocamora, Nicholson, Wilson & Hinkle, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Durham, NC
attorneys.bio:
A native of Opelika, Alabama, Catherine joined the firm in 2011 upon her family’s move to Durham. She is a graduate of David Lipscomb University in Nashville, Tennessee, with a B.A. in English, magna cum laude (2001), and earned her law degree from Vanderbilt University in 2005 where she was an Honors Scholar and served as Executive Articles Editor for the Vanderbilt Journal of Transnational Law. She also earned a Masters of Theological Studies from Vanderbilt University Divinity School in 2005 as well.

Upon graduation, Catherine practiced with the Birmingham, Alabama law firm of Sirote & Permutt, P.C., from 2005 to 2011, working exclusively in the areas of trusts and estates. She is a member of the American, North Carolina, Alabama, and Durham Bar Associations and is a member of the Estate Planning and Fiduciary Law Section of the North Carolina Bar. She also serves on the Board of the Fourteenth Judicial District Bar, the Durham County Bar Association, and the Durham Bar Foundation.

Catherine’s practice focuses on estate planning, special needs planning, guardianships, taxation law, and trust and estate litigation. Her special needs practice includes assisting with planning for family members with special needs and also the post-litigation establishment of special needs trusts designed to receive personal injury awards.
